In ACC After Dark action, Stanford hosts NC State at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, Calif., on Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Wolfpack are 6.5-point road favorites, and my NC State vs. Stanford prediction and college football picks expect CJ Bailey to pick apart one of the Power Four's worst defenses. TOP PICK Who will win NC State vs Stanford: NC State -6.5 Stanford has been completely uncompetitive in four of its last five FBS games and is 1-5 ATS since the start of September. While NC State isn't a powerhouse, the Wolfpack have enough offense to cover up to -8.5 on the road . The Cardinal have lost four of their last five FBS games by at least 28 points and scored seven or fewer in all four (they were outscored 115-10 in their last two FBS games) . With a defense that's ranked 127th in success rate (50.1%) , Stanford's offense won't be able to keep up with the Wolfpack. NC State has scored 31+ points in three of its last four FBS games, all against defenses ranked higher by SP+ than Stanford's (111th). Plus, the Wolfpack are coming off a bye week and should be well rested for the West Coast trip. NC State vs Stanford Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 NC State and Stanford have struggling defenses, which have helped them consistently hit the Over this season. The Wolfpack and Cardinal are a combined 9-4 to the Over, and I like it to hit at 55.5 or better . Stanford's defense has the lowest havoc rate in the ACC (11.3%) and is allowing the second-most yards per game in the Power Four (452) . NC State's defense isn't all that much better, though, ranking 124th in net EPA per play and 133rd in EPA per pass. These two defenses bend and break, ranking the worst in the conference in points per opportunity on defense, though Stanford (5.06) is significantly worse than NC State (3.94). NC State vs Stanford combo Stanford is one of the worst teams in college football, and it doesn't look like Andrew Luck and Tavita Pritchard will be turning things around anytime soon. Though Davis Warren has been efficient at QB, the Cardinal have a dreadful defense that ranks outside the top 115 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and available yards percentage (57.3%). Even against an NC State defense giving up 27.7 points per game, Stanford won't be able to keep this close at home against David Doeren's team. The Wolfpack's passing game will be too much, and I have NC State winning 33-24 . Star Exclusive Pack Power Predictions for NC State vs. Stanford football in Week 8 NC State football is back on the road for the first time since Week 3 on Friday night, with the Wolfpack looking to snap a six-game road losing streak against Stanford. Here's how our staff sees the game going down. RALEIGH, N.C. -- NC State football is back on the road for the first time since Week 3 on Friday night, with the Wolfpack looking to snap a six-game road losing streak against Stanford. Here's how our staff sees the game going down. Michael Clark NC State's injury issues went from bad to worse during a bye week with news of multiple other starters who are out for Friday's game. Losing three fifths of the offensive line -- two of which are out for the season -- along with two important playmakers is certainly a problem going into this one. However, the Wolfpack still should be able to find a way to beat a really bad Stanford team. I believe the Cardinal will put up a fight in the first half, but State makes a few big plays in the fourth quarter after preparing for the time change all week and wins by two scores. Final Prediction: NC State 38, Stanford 28 Charlie Gribble The bye week has come and gone for NC State -- a sad reality for some in the Wolfpack fanbase -- as Dave Doeren and company embark on a cross-country trip to Palo Alto to take on Stanford. It's still hard to put into words where this program currently stands, with a head coach officially halfway through his 14th season at the helm and coming off yet another second-half collapse, this time at the hands of a less-funded Wake Forest program led by a head coach in just his second year in Winston-Salem. Regardless, the Wolfpack need to take advantage of what should be some winnable, must-have games down the stretch. That starts Friday night, with the Cardinal coming in ranked dead last in the ACC in both total offense and total defense. Even with key absences on both sides of the ball for the Pack, headlined by Duke Scott's absence in the backfield, NC State has more talent across the board. Anything less than a convincing win against a Stanford team that hasn't reached the postseason since 2018 would raise serious questions about the future direction of the program's leadership -- as if those questions aren't already being asked. I expect the Wolfpack to come out to a somewhat sluggish start given the time-zone difference. However, CJ Bailey will open things up in the final 30 minutes to lead NC State to a victory and, more notably in my eyes, a cover against what I view as a low touchdown spread set by Vegas. Final Prediction: NC State 41, Stanford 28 Terrence McCallen The Pack heads west at 3-3, coming off a bye that couldn't have come at a better time after the 38-14 loss to Wake Forest. That one stung, and the second half was about as ugly as it gets for CJ Bailey. But two weeks to reset and a trip to Stanford is a pretty good recipe for getting right. Start with the Cardinal defense, because it's been bad. Stanford is giving up 36.6 points per game (133rd in FBS) and 452 yards per game (134th). It's been especially soft on the ground, allowing 196.6 rushing yards per game and 20 rushing touchdowns, which ranks 137th in the country. That's why I'm not worried about the run game, even without Duke Scott. Against a front like this, Gause should find room. That opens everything up for Bailey, and I expect him to bounce back with an efficient night. And if the Pack gets inside the 20, Stanford isn't stopping it. Opponents are scoring on 96.4% of their red zone trips. On the other side, Stanford's offense has struggled to score all year at 18.3 points per game, and its run game ranks 131st. If NC State's defense makes the Cardinal one-dimensional, this one gets away from them in the second half. A 10:30 p.m. kickoff on the West Coast is never easy, but I think the Pack takes care of business and gets back above .500. Final Prediction: NC State 35, Stanford 10 Spencer Thomas NC State is approaching a do-or-die point in its season. At 3-3 (1-2 ACC), the Wolfpack has already fallen well short of expectations. A blowout loss in Week 0, a collapse against Vanderbilt, and a disappointing showing against Wake Forest have put the team in a tough position heading into the second half of the season. With six games remaining, there's still time to turn things around, starting tomorrow night against Stanford. Battling a growing list of injuries, NC State will need a complete performance in all three phases of the game to come away with a win. Despite Stanford entering as a 6.5-point underdog, I expect this matchup to be much closer than the spread suggests. Special teams could ultimately be the difference, so don't be surprised if Kanoah Vinesett ends up playing the role of hero for the Wolfpack tomorrow night. Final Prediction: NC State 31 Stanford 28 The good news is NC State defeated the bye week. The bad news? It came away with more players on the injury report and several key pieces now out for the season. Such is life for the Wolfpack. This week, however, is a chance for State to get back on track and finally come away with a road win. Despite not having Duke Scott in the backfield and a depleted offensive line, this still feels like a Stanford defense Davion Gause and Co. will have success against and establish the run game early. I believe NC State establishes the run early and controls the clock in the first half. Stanford then stages a comeback in the second half before CJ Bailey seals his first road win since the Wake Forest game last season with a methodical drive late to come away with a 28-21 win. Final Prediction: NC State 28, Wake Forest 21 Even with the cross-country flight and late kickoff, NC State has no excuse not to take care of business against Stanford on Friday night. The Cardinal have been one of the worst teams in the conference to this point, and coming off a bye week, the Wolfpack must start winning the so-called "easy games" from here on out. The Pack are currently 0-2 on the road and could use a win to prove to themselves that they can get the job done away from Carter-Finley, even if it comes against a struggling opponent. State will once again be extremely shorthanded despite having a full week off, presenting another challenge the Pack must overcome. Even with multiple key starters sidelined, it would be disastrous if the Wolfpack can't get a win this week. At this point in the season, dropping a game like this would only add to the pressure on Dave Doeren and raise more questions about the direction of the program. Final Prediction: NC State 38, Stanford 17 Look, I know NC State is down a ton of key players on offense, as we've established by all of the other predictions above. The Wolfpack has struggled mightily to get the ground game going, has issues maintaining leads and lacks overall explosiveness on offense -- while giving up way too many explosive plays on defense. But this Stanford team has been nearly non-competitive against Power Four competition this season outside of beating a bad Georgia Tech team at home. Even with all of the travel, time change and injuries the Wolfpack is dealing with, it should be fully prepared for this moment out of a bye week, right? Right?! No team in the country has allowed more "defensive bust plays" than Stanford at 111. Only seven teams have missed more tackles than Stanford's 0.39 per play. Only one team has less sacks than Stanford at just four through seven games. And that same defensive unit has allowed 196.6 rushing yards per game -- which ranks last in the ACC and 124th in the country. This feels like a breakout game for Davion Gause, Deandre Desinor or *someone* Doeren is hiding off the depth chart. And when that person gets going, the passing game should take off under CJ Bailey and allow the Wolfpack to roll to a convincing win before heading back to Raleigh to face another west coast team next Saturday. home.blurb: Coming into the game, the Phoenix decided to shake up their offense and start junior quarterback T.J. Crews IV for the first time since a Sept. 12 loss at Rhode Island (4-3, 1-2 CAA). This was to little avail: Stanford’s defense forced a quick three-and-out on the opening drive as Crews’ first two passing attempts were disrupted. The Stanford offense once again found its footing by the third drive of the second half, when a good punt return by sophomore punt returner Liam Thorpe set the Cardinal up at midfield. Three Ford rushes later, Warren would throw a beautiful 27-yard back-shoulder ball to senior running back Sedrick Irvin for the third touchdown of the day. While the 83-degree heat and sun beating down on the eastern side of the stands might have initially subdued the student section, the fans who did show up got to see what this team believes they are truly capable of. “I think for the first time in a minute, we started to put together some really good football,” said junior linebacker Sam Mattingly after a second consecutive week leading the team with five tackles. Mattingly, alongside senior safety Jay Green, were instrumental in holding the Phoenix offense to only 52 passing yards and scoreless through three quarters. Incompletions and miscues would be a theme for both teams as they settled in. Stanford would go 64 yards down the field before sixth-year kicker Emmet Kenney missed a 35-yard field goal attempt. Elon responded by attempting to lean on freshman running back Kamerin McDowell-Moore, who alone accounted for 971 of Elon’s 2,573 total offensive yards going into the game. The Phoenix would make it 44 yards in 10 plays before their own kicker, junior Luke Barnes, came up short on his 54-yard field goal attempt. It was not until the Cardinal’s second drive that they found their stride. Junior running back Micah Ford broke tackles on a critical third-and-nine early in the drive, before sixth-year quarterback Davis Warren uncorked a 32-yard pass to sophomore wide receiver JonAnthony Hall to set up first-and-goal at the Elon seven-yard line. On the first play of the second quarter, Ford would punch it in for the touchdown. There were still some offensive issues. In between two five-play Elon drives that were stopped by a combination of defense and errant throws by Crews, the Cardinal would sputter after losing two yards on second down and failing to convert a third-and-six. In contrast, on the next Stanford offensive drive, Warren would work the mid-range passing game with poise down into the red zone. Head coach Tavita Pritchard noted that Warren excels at “staying the course.” “When some of those plays do start to go our way, he’s ready for those moments; he’s not pressing,” Pritchard said, also highlighting Warren’s ability to avoid turnovers. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Indiana looks to rebound from a loss to Ohio State, while Michigan begins again at quarterback Getty Images The Tommy Carr era in Ann Arbor will officially get underway this Saturday when the freshman quarterback makes his first career start at home against No. 6 Indiana . Carr led a second-half comeback last week against Penn State after former five-star recruit Bryce Underwood was benched, and Michigan made the decision to fully turn the operation over to Carr against an extremely good Indiana defense. That will present a major challenge for Carr, but it also shows Michigan's faith in him as the best option against the defending champs. Indiana comes into the game trying to shake off the frustration of a loss at home to Ohio State last week, coming a literal foot away from a win had Nick Marsh been able to keep his feet in bounds on a wide-open fourth-down pass from Josh Hoover . The Hoosiers need to refocus after the disappointment of their first loss in two years, as they head into the Big House to face a Michigan team that may not be elite on offense but will still present a stiff test for an Indiana offense that's been out of sync recently. The Hoosiers are 7.5-point road favorites, but the Wolverines suddenly have a bit of life after last week's win, and the excitement for a new quarterback will create a lively atmosphere in Ann Arbor. Michigan vs. Indiana: Need to know Tommy Carr's first start: Carr took over for Bryce Underwood at halftime against Penn State and performed solidly, leading three Michigan touchdown drives -- that came off three Penn State turnovers. While he only threw for 47 yards, playing complementary football and cashing in on great defensive plays to turn them into points is a major step forward for this Michigan offense. However, doing that against a bad Penn State team is one thing; now Carr will face an Indiana defense that's among the best in the country. He'll be tasked with not turning the ball over and taking what's in front of him, but Indiana will know that as well, and Michigan might have to let Carr turn it loose a couple of times down the field if they're going to force the Hoosiers off the line of scrimmage. Michigan knows this will be an extremely difficult first start for Carr and will likely try to protect him with quick concepts and a run-heavy approach, but if they want to pull off the upset, Carr is going to have to deliver a couple big plays Indiana's not expecting. Can Indiana establish a rhythm?: A stop-start offense has been a problem all season for Indiana, and while they escaped the first six games without it costing them, it finally caught up in Columbus. Now they face a Michigan defense that is also excellent and will present plenty of challenges, and Josh Hoover will have to prove he can move the ball consistently through the air. Indiana's offense has been predicated much more on the big play than they'd like this season, as Hoover has been able to create explosives in the passing game to Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh. However, consistency has been lacking, and that's kept the Hoosiers from pulling away from opponents as they did a year ago. Against Ohio State, Hoover threw for 296 yards, but completed just 20 of 40 passes to do so. He will need to figure out how to be sharper in the underneath and intermediate passing game if Indiana's going to have a chance of repeating, and that starts this week given the challenge Michigan will present up front. Elite run defenses: The Hoosiers and Wolverines are two of the nation's best defenses against the run, and that presents real problems for offenses that want to lean on their rushing attacks. Indiana struggled to get anything going against Ohio State, even with Turbo Richard back in the lineup, and they'll be up against it again with a Michigan defense that allows a paltry 2.68 yards per carry. One of the six teams better than Michigan against the run is Indiana, allowing just 2.28 yards per carry, which will put even more pressure on Carr to produce through the air in his first start. The team that can establish some kind of ground game will gain an advantage in this one, but there's a real possibility that neither can break through the walls of these defensive fronts. Where to watch Michigan vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, Michigan TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Michigan vs. Indiana prediction, picks We've got two elite run defenses, one inconsistent passing attack and one freshman making his first start. That is a recipe for a low-scoring battle. Michigan has played five games against teams not named UTEP , and all five games have finished with fewer than 40 points. Indiana's last two games have finished in the 30s as well, as they've faced the two best defenses on their schedule thus far, and it's hard to see a game flow here leading to anything approaching a shootout. The fear here is the potential for defensive scores, but even so, give me the under in Ann Arbor for the second straight week. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for Indiana football vs. Michigan: Josh Hoover will have a day
picks.blurb: Indiana (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten), for the first time in a long time, is looking to get back on track. It’ll have an opportunity to do just that at Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) after falling last week to Ohio State at home. Can the Hoosiers do it ? That would be a hard yes if two of these bold predictions come true and one doesn’t. 3 bold predictions for Indiana at Michigan Michigan doesn’t score a touchdown The Wolverines, despite their abysmal offense through the first half of the season, have scored at least two touchdowns in every Big Ten game thus far. Expect that streak to be snapped by Indiana. The Hoosiers are simply a different test than anything Michigan has seen. True freshman Tommy Carr is poised to get his first career start on Saturday. And while it may be the best decision for the Wolverines, it couldn’t come against a tougher opponent. Indiana is going to speed Carr up, force Michigan to rely on its ground attack and then bottle that up (currently surrendering a Big Ten-best 2.3 yards per carry and just 75.4 total yards per game). The Wolverines might be able to trek into Hoosiers territory on occasion, but never into the end zone. The Hoosiers don’t crack 100 yards on the ground A few signs point in the right direction for Indiana’s run game on Saturday (at least from a total-yardage perspective). First of all, the Hoosiers run the ball a lot – and they’ve been very good at it in the Curt Cignetti era. In Indiana’s first two Big Ten outings, it registered 271 yards and 329 yards on the ground, respectively. Also, against Michigan, the expectation is that the Hoosiers should be leading most of the game. And there is no better way to nurse a lead than run the football. On the flip side, though, Indiana has managed a combined 138 rushing yards on 51 carries over the past two games. The offensive line has failed to get any push and the running backs haven’t been able to find any holes. Chunk plays, explosive plays – the Hoosiers can’t get anything positive (didn’t even have a single rush over 10 yards against Ohio State). The other bad news: Michigan’s rushing defense is elite. It allows just 2.7 yards per carry and 89.7 yards per game. This, unfortunately for Indiana, is a stoppable-force-meets-immovable-object scenario. Josh Hoover throws for three touchdowns Save for the Rutgers win – which, should that even count as Big Ten play? – quarterback Josh Hoover hasn’t thrown for three touchdowns in a league game. That may be set to change on Saturday, though. Michigan’s defense is flat-out dominant. But its lone vulnerability is defending the pass. Iowa’s Hank Brown threw for 227 yards and two scores. Penn State’s Rocco Becht slung it for 267 yards and a touchdown through the air. And, all due respect to both of those gunslingers, but neither is at the same level as Hoover, nor do they have the unreal weapons Hoover has on the outside. Expect Hoover and his stud wide receiver duo of Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh to feast against Michigan, especially considering the ongoing rushing struggles for the Hoosiers’ offense. My Indiana vs. Michigan prediction backs the Wolverines to keep it close during Saturday afternoon's Big Ten showdown. With Bryce Underwood taking a seat and Tommy Carr making his first collegiate start, Michigan's offense could get a refreshing change of pace. However, I still expect both defenses to dominate from start to finish. Find out why I'm backing the Wolverines in my latest college football picks ahead of Saturday's noon ET kickoff on FOX. TOP PICK Who will win Indiana vs Michigan: Michigan +7.5 If this is the end for Bryce Underwood and the start of the Tommy Carr era, Michigan is the play on Saturday. The freshman threw for just 47 yards while completing five of seven attempts after replacing Underwood during a win over Penn State. He also rushed for 36 yards and found pay dirt in the fourth quarter. Anything is better than forcing Underwood out there, especially when he's been a turnover machine. The Indiana Hoosiers are coming off a tough loss to the Ohio State Buckeyes, a game they were just inches away from winning. Some will see that heartbreak and run to bet the Hoosiers this week, but this Michigan team catching 7.5 points is too good to pass up. The Wolverines boast a defense allowing the fewest yards per play in the country , the second-fewest total yards, and just over 16 points per game. I snagged +7.5, but I endorse Michigan down to +7. Indiana vs Michigan Over/Under pick: Under 41.5 Look at that beautiful key number of 41 and the hook! For Michigan to cover in this matchup, the Under will need to be the play, even with Carr running the show. With this being the freshman's first collegiate start, he's likely to hit some speed bumps along the way. Head coach Kyle Whittingham will probably take a more conservative approach, leaning on designed runs while Carr continues to develop into the passer this team needs him to be going forward. Indiana has done an incredible job limiting scoring this season, with Big Ten opponents averaging just 18.5 points per game against the Hoosiers . I envision a 20-17 ballgame at its ceiling. I'd take this under down to 40, at most. Indiana vs Michigan combo This game script sets up nicely for a correlated parlay. Published Oct. 22, 2026 2:49 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Geoff Schwartz FOX Sports Betting Analyst Indiana goes on the road to face the greatest rival of its newest rival, and Utah and Houston will face off in a game that has CFP and Big 12 title implications. On the field, college football is in a great place. Here's what I'm picking in Week 8. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . No. 6 Indiana @ Michigan There are two types of wagers for me. There are the kind that I love and those don't tend to cash as often. Then there are the wagers that scare me, and while it is uncomfortable placing said wagers and watching said game, those tend to hit. Wagering on Michigan in this game scares me. Michigan is the right side for many reasons. The first is that Indiana is off its first loss in over a year and a half. How does this squad handle losing at home with all the world watching? And they lost in a way we haven’t seen often — with Curt Cignetti at the helm. Mistakes, turnovers and a receiver just not getting his foot inbounds on the final offensive play of the game cost IU, but the Hoosiers also haven't been able to run the ball this season, which was far from the case last year. It was just 2.8 yards per attempt for their running backs against Ohio State and 2.4 against Nebraska the week before. In addition, Josh Hoover isn’t Fernando Mendoza at quarterback, which we already knew. Hoover can’t make things right like Mendoza could. The Michigan defense is first in yards per play, even though the Wolverines haven't played anyone like Indiana. Still, Michigan’s pass rush is good, and I’d imagine it will try to pressure Hoover into mistakes. It’s also Indiana’s third straight week of playing a physical defense. How do the Hoosiers hold up on the road? I think Indiana’s offense will score in the low 20s. The Indiana defense is still fantastic this season. It is ninth in points per drive and doesn't have many weaknesses. Maybe it allows some success rushing the ball and doesn't rush the passer quite the same as last season. However, it’s still a formidable unit. What worries me the most about this wager is the Michigan offense, which was dead with quarterback Bryce Underwood. Michigan benched Underwood for true freshman quarterback Tommy Carr last week and the offense scored 21 second-half points, appearing competent with Carr under center. However, Carr only threw the ball seven times for 47 yards. Not exactly an elite passing performance. What can Tommy Carr produce for the Wolverines against the Hoosiers? (Getty Images) Now, Carr has to play Indiana’s defense and IU had a week to prepare. I could easily see this Michigan offense being overwhelmed with a true freshman under fire. Still, it is clear the Wolverines are playing more confidently with Carr at QB and I do believe they can score enough, maybe in the high teens, to cover this game. I think I’ll need 17 points from Michigan and I will get it. Schwartz's Pick: Michigan +7 No. 14 Houston @ No. 10 Utah What an awesome Big 12 matchup on Saturday night. The winner of this game has a leg up in the Big 12 title race and a spot in Dallas for the conference championship game. I see a game with points, many of them potentially coming late. But nonetheless, I expect scoring. Utah’s defense has been a hallmark of its program for years, and while it appears to be good this season, I’m not quite sure. It is 26th in yards per play, but the best offense it has faced is 63rd-ranked Kansas, which scored 24 points and passed for 333 yards. Last weekend, Colorado scored 24 points, the most it has scored against an FBS opponent all season. Utah can't rush the passer. It is 66th in pressure rate and 112th in sacks. That's why teams have passed the ball on the Utes. Houston’s offense is well-prepared considering it has already faced Texas Tech on the road and put up 458 yards of offense. The Cougars also just scored 35 against Oklahoma State. Houston’s offensive line is outstanding. It is fifth in rushing success rate and top-25 in pressure rate. The Cougars' offense is first in the sport on third down. Third down has been a strong point for Connor Weigman and the Cougars this season (Getty Images). Houston’s defense is not its strong suit, ranking 99th in yards per play and 124th in percent of plays that go 20+ yards. It is also awful in the red zone, which isn't a great sign against a Utah offense that can attack you in so many ways. week, the #6 Indiana Hoosiers (6-1) are on the road with no time to sulk. This week the Hoosiers head to The Big House and take on a rested Michigan Wolverines (4-2) team. Michigan enters with a new sense of hope for the rest of the season. The Wolverines are fresh off a bye week and announced that Tommy Carr will be starting against Indiana, not the $12 million dollar man Bryce Underwood . Carr replaced Underwood in the second half against Penn State and led a comeback charge to win 21-18 after Michigan trailed 3-0 at the half. Carr had 83 total yards and a rushing touchdown in the second half of the win, which was encouraging for Michigan supporters. On the flip side, this will be Carr’s first collegiate start, and it’s against Curt Cignetti and Indiana coming off a loss (33-3 record with Cignetti). Yikes. Throw him to the wolves why don’t ya? Indiana is still favored to make the College Football Playoff despite the loss to Ohio State. The Hoosiers’ only ranked game remaining is against USC on Nov. 14, and the Trojans play Ohio State the week prior, so it’s a good spot for Indiana. Indiana likely finishes the regular season 11-1, and it’s a rematch between the Buckeyes and Hoosiers in the Big Ten Championship Game. The only question then would be: is Julian Sayin back? That’s a question and conversation for another day. The Hoosiers’ run game was stalled in the loss to Ohio State. Indiana ran for 73 yards on 29 carries (2.5 ypc) and recorded zero explosive runs. The offense relied heavily on Josh Hoover , Charlie Becker , and Nick Marsh to cook. Becker and Marsh caught 12 of Hoover’s 20 completions (60%) and 222 of the 296 passing yards (75%). Hoover had a season-high 40 pass attempts, his only game over 30, and Indiana shouldn’t have to pass as much this week, or again for the rest of the regular season. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Tommy Carr , brother of Notre Dame’s CJ Carr, will get the start. What to expect from Carr and the Wolverines’ offense is up in the air. Carr had seven drives to work with in the second half versus Penn State and finished with 47 passing yards, 36 rushing yards, and a rushing score. Michigan scored 21 second-half points after trailing 3-0 at halftime. Michigan’s Team Total for this game is 16.5, and Carr is projected at Over or Under 137.5 passing yards and 15.5 rushing yards. That doesn’t sound very promising coming off the bye week. Michigan did run for 211 yards and three touchdowns against Penn State, but the Hoosiers’ rush defense ranks first in rush defense per PFF. Michigan Player to Watch on Offense: QB Tommy Carr Carr led the second-half comeback charge against Penn State and scored on three out of seven drives despite not totaling 100 yards in the half. After paying Bryce Underwood $12 million, Carr comes in with much lower expectations and should thrive over the next few games, but this is a rough spot. The positive is that Michigan had a bye week to work with Carr and see what makes him comfortable, but making your first career start against Curt Cignetti, as Indiana is coming off only the third loss in Cignetti’s Hoosiers coaching career, does not sound ideal for Carr. The Michigan Wolverines Defense: The Michigan defense forced Penn State’s Rocco Becht into three turnovers (2 INT, 1 FUM) in the last game and held the rushing attack to 65 yards on 30 carries (2.2 ypc). Penn State scored twice in the fourth quarter to pull the score within one possession, but Michigan shut the door the following possessions and held Penn State to four punts in the first half. Michigan ranks second-best in the country in rush defense per PFF, behind only Indiana, and the Wolverines are top 25 in pressure (11th) and coverage grades (18th). The defense will have to carry them on Saturday to stay within striking distance. Michigan Player to Watch on Defense: DL John Henry Daley John Henry Daley entered the bye week on a four-game sack streak and has thrived at Michigan. Daley played for Whittingham at Utah the last two seasons (12.5 sacks) after starting his career at BYU. Daley’s stock has been rising this season after a career-high 11.5 sacks with the Utes. Daley has 4.0 sacks over five games in his pocket with 1.5 versus Oklahoma, 1.0 versus UTEP and Penn State, plus a 0.5 sack against Iowa. away.headline: Ohio State QB1 Battle Updated by Ryan Day After Julian Sayin's Injury vs. Indiana
away.blurb: The importance of the quarterback battle extends beyond the Buckeyes' next game against USC, as Day told reporters Tuesday it is "doubtful" Sayin will return for the regular season following his setback in the win over the Hoosiers. Bleacher Report • 9h AD Calls Out Wizards Crowd 😅 Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College Football Ohio State's quarterback battle following Julian Sayin's injury against Indiana will be one of the most consequential storylines of the College Football Playoff race down the stretch of the season, and head coach Ryan Day provided an update Thursday. "Ultimately, I make the final decision, but you take the input from the coaches, take the input from our personnel department and then the players as well," Day told reporters when discussing Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair competing for the starting role. "They're the ones in the huddle with these guys. That's what it comes down to." That Day is taking feedback from players is notable, and it's safe to assume one of those players he talks to will be Jeremiah Smith. Smith is arguably the best player in college football, and getting the ball into the hands of the Heisman Trophy favorite will be the most important thing that either Fahey or St. Clair can do when they are under center. Ohio State lost a Heisman Trophy finalist from last year and one of its offensive leaders with the injury. What's more, an already difficult schedule with remaining games against USC, Oregon, Nebraska, Michigan and Northwestern is now all the more daunting without its starting quarterback who completed 68.2 percent of his passes for 2,007 yards, 19 touchdowns and four interceptions prior to the injury. After all, he is a true freshman and was a 3-star prospect, per 247Sports' composite rankings. By comparison, St. Clair was a 5-star recruit in the 2025 class, per 247Sports' composite rankings, and has been on campus for far longer. Ohio State turned to Fahey to finish the game against Indiana following Sayin's injury, but the timing of its bye week ahead of the next contest gives Day and the coaching staff more time to evaluate the position moving forward with the context now changed. home.headline: Michigan lists six starters, including Rod Moore, as questionable vs. Indiana
home.blurb: Moore, the Wolverines’ starting safety and one of four team captains, center Jake Guarnera, right guard Brady Norton and tackle Blake Frazier are all listed as questionable for Saturday’s game against No. 6 Indiana on Saturday (12 p.m., FOX). Michigan submitted its first player availability report of the week to the Big Ten on Wednesday, with seven players ruled out, another seven listed as questionable and one as probable. Moore had to be carted to the locker room during the Wolverines’ 21-18 win over Penn State last Saturday, an injury that appeared to occur when he laid out for his third-quarter interception. Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham wouldn’t categorize Moore’s injury as particularly serious after the game, calling it “nothing that’s long term” and “he’ll be OK.” Norton missed last week’s game with an undisclosed injury, a blow to Michigan’s already-depleted offensive line. Guarnera, on the player report again this week, was listed as a game-time decision but played. Frazier, a starter at left tackle during Michigan’s first two games and right tackle for the last four, is new to the report this week. Elsewhere along the offensive line, starting right tackle Andrew Sprague will miss his fifth consecutive game with an undisclosed issue while sophomore Andrew Babalola, still waiting to make his collegiate debut, is probable. Another surprise: Michigan starting defensive tackle Enow Etta is questionable. The Wolverines’ defensive line has been a strength of the team this year, ranking 13th nationally in rushing defense (90 yards per game), and not having Etta would be a major blow up front. Starting defensive end Dom Nichols is questionable to play for a fourth straight game, though he’s appeared in the last three. home.headline: Michigan injury updates: Rod Moore ‘OK’ after being carted off in win
home.blurb: The Wolverines were down a second starting offensive lineman, guard Brady Norton, while center Jake Guarnera and guard Nathan Efobi both played through injuries in Saturday’s 21-18 victory at Michigan Stadium . Guarnera especially, having been listed as a game-time decision two hours before kickoff. “Everyone has something going on at this point in the season,” starting tackle Blake Frazier said. “I’m super proud of him. He was straining all week to make sure that he was giving himself the best opportunity to be out there with us today.” ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Michigan football continues to limp its way through the schedule, and the win over Penn State was no different. Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) started backup Avery Gach at right guard while welcoming sixth offensive lineman Manuel Beigel back to the lineup. The Wolverines were able to run for a season-high 211 yards and three touchdowns, much of that coming in the second half with backup Tommy Carr at quarterback. In-game, though, the Wolverines had to deal with a couple of scares. Safety Rod Moore had to be carted off the field in the third quarter after intercepting a Rocco Becht pass; his first turnover of the season. “Should be OK,” Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham said. “It’s nothing major. Now, will he be ready for the next game? That’s debatable, but it’s nothing that’s long term.” That’s good news for Moore, who returned in full this season following a two-year rehab from a torn ACL and meniscus in his knee. He’s started all six games this season and is one of two captains on defense. Meanwhile, cornerback Jyaire Hill was missing in the secondary toward the end of the game, and Whittingham suggested an injury kept him from playing. “But it doesn’t appear to be anything — kind of like Rod — long term,” Whittingham said. Hill struggled in coverage against Penn State receiver Chase Sowell, who caught 11 passes for 151 yards and a touchdown and drew a pair of holding penalties against the senior defensive back. “That receiver is a good receiver,” Whittingham said. “A big, physical kid. I thought we were a little soft in pass defense this game. We needed to get up and challenge a little more, get in the receiver’s face and be a little bit more aggressive in that respect.” To illustrate how beaten up Michigan is, Whittingham said as many as six starters would have been sidelined last week had the Wolverines played a game. They were on a bye instead, giving the team enough time to get some players back in time. “It was good to get those guys healthy and be able to get them to this game and perform,” Whittingham said. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Getty Images One week after stunning No. 1 Georgia , Auburn will try to replicate that effort against No. 18 LSU . Auburn will have the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd on it side, but the team faces an uphill battle in the pursuit of two major upsets. Going into its open date, Auburn was coming off a loss to Tennessee and needed something to build upon. An upset of the No. 1 team in the country on the road will certainly suffice, and now Alex Golesh must find a way to sustain that momentum. If Auburn is going to give itself a shot to slay SEC dragons in consecutive weeks, it will need to put the game on the shoulders of Byrum Brown again. He totaled 265 yards and a pair of touchdowns against the Bulldogs. On the other hand, LSU will have to be wary of entering a hostile environment given its recent history. The team has lost both of its road games this season, and Lane Kiffin's struggles away from home date back to when he first accepted the Ole Miss job. The Baton Rouge-based Tigers just shut out a shorthanded Mississippi State team in Death Valley, and Sam Leavitt played the first clean game of his LSU tenure. He'll need to replicate that performance in Auburn. Before this battle of the Tigers begins, we have everything you need to know about the matchup. LSU vs. Auburn: Need to know LSU's road woes: LSU is the clear favorite in this game, but it has struggled to win road games lately. The Tigers have dropped eight straight road games, which is the third-longest streak in school history. LSU is 0-2 on the road this fall, and Kiffin hasn't fared well away from home throughout his SEC coaching career. Between stops at Tennessee, Ole Miss and LSU, Kiffin is 14-16. Winning on the road is hard, but LSU can't make it even harder. Run, Bryum, run: If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense. That worked last week in Athens, as Brown toted the rock on 26 attempts, which included five sacks. The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs. Auburn trying to go back-to-back: Can Auburn pull off two stunners in a row? The Tigers haven't picked up wins over ranked teams in consecutive weeks since they rattled off three straight against Georgia, Alabama and Missouri in 2013. The trouble is that Auburn hasn't played well at home against ranked opponents of late, which is somewhat surprising given the general mystique around Jordan-Hare Stadium. The team is 1-9 in its last 10 home games against top-25 teams. picks.headline: Why this analyst predicts Auburn to lose by double digits against LSU
picks.blurb: The Auburn Tigers are red-hot after their stunning win against No. 1 Georgia last week, but they will not have any time to rest on their laurels, as up next for Alex Golesh’s squad is a big-time matchup with LSU, and early predictions are not in the Tigers’ favor. As it stands, the Tigers are a seven-point underdog to their rival Tigers, though CBS Sports’ Austin Nivison believes the Tigers will lose by at least 10 points . Here’s why. “What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable,” he wrote. “Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double digits.” In fact, every CBS analyst polled about the game took Lane Kiffin’s squad to win straight-up, but a few, like Chip Patterson and David Cobb, predicted the Tigers to at least cover the spread. It’s certainly a difficult matchup for the Tigers, who could be experiencing what Kiffin called ‘relief syndrome’ after their win against Georgia. There is a path to the Tigers winning this game, though, and it seems to run through Byrum Brown. “If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense,” Nivison continued. “That worked last week in Athens... The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs.” Brown seemed to have been contained a bit in earlier games, as his number was called for design plays quite rarely, but against the Dawgs, Auburn offensive coordinator Joel Gordon leaned on Brown’s legs to get the Tigers’ offense moving. It worked to great effect last week, but LSU will now be even more prepared for Brown’s dual-threat nature, which adds a layer of complexity to the Tigers’ playcalling this week. The Tigers, coming off a marquee win, are looking to continue their momentum, and having home-field advantage should play a big part in their matchup with Kiffin’s Tigers. However, LSU has answers for most of Auburn’s offensive production, so the Tigers will likely need to get creative if they want to emerge from the Tiger Bowl with a win. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:12 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads All of a sudden, the SEC is up for grabs, and Auburn and LSU had a lot to do with that. Ten SEC teams fall into the 4-1 to 2-2 range after Auburn pulled off a stunning 27-24 win at Georgia last week. The rest of the AU Tiger schedule is challenging, but if you can beat Georgia in Sanford Stadium, the bar gets set a little higher. LSU lost both of its road games – Ole Miss and Kentucky – but it's been an unstoppable force at home, destroying Clemson by 41, Texas A&M by 29, and beating Mississippi State 31-0 last week. The Bayou Bengal Tigers are still among the most dangerous and talented teams in the country on the right day, but, like Auburn, one more loss and that's about it for the SEC and College Football Playoff dreams. LSU vs Auburn: Quick Hits LSU gets a nasty run over the next three games, but Alabama and Texas are home games before going to Tennessee. Auburn goes to Ole Miss next, and three of the last four SEC games are on the road. LSU beat Auburn 48-18 when the two last met in 2023 and has won six of the last eight games. The Auburn offense wants to move at a lightning-fast pace, and Lane Kiffin's attack is at its best when it's going 150 miles per hour. The one big difference is control of the tempo. LSU is amazing at dominating the time of possession battle, and it should hold the ball for large chunks of time. Auburn is 133rd in the nation, keeping the ball for fewer than 27 minutes per game. As much as the offense matters, though, it's the LSU defense that has to keep Auburn from getting out of third gear. LSU is second in the nation in sacks, and AU can't keep quarterback Byrum Brown from getting popped. Why Auburn Will Win It really is impressive. LSU looks and plays like it has 14 guys on the field who are all twice as fast as everyone else … at home. The LSU offense wasn't too bad in the losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky, but the defense occasionally played like it didn't attend the last three classes before the test. It's not a coincidence. LSU has allowed more than 145 passing yards just two times this season. Take a wild guess which teams got it going through the air. In case you were wondering, the 21-15 win over Vanderbilt is the only time Auburn failed to throw for at least 145 yards. LSU vs Auburn Prediction, Betting Lines Let's get it out of the way. Really, how did Auburn beat Georgia? First of all, Auburn is just that good. But also, it actually held its own in the time of possession battle – the defense held up and wasn't gassed late. That, and it helped to get be +3 in turnover margin. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt will throw his customary interception – although he didn't give one away for the first time all year in last week's win over Mississippi State – but LSU's control of the clock and the narrative on the lines will be enough to finally get a road win. It feels like everyone in the country is feeling the same way about this weekend's matchup between Tennessee and South Carolina in Columbia. Everyone is expecting the Vols to come out flat after their big win against Alabama and have a letdown game against the Gamecocks. Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray is picking South Carolina to win . So is former Alabama quarterback Greg McElroy . Another former SEC star who is picking South Carolina is David Pollack, a former Georgia standout. Pollack has the Gamecocks winning 27-20 on Saturday. "South Carolina does a really good job of running the football and staying out of obvious third and long," said Pollack. "Have you seen this Matt Fuller guy for South Carolina? I really like this dude. Between him and (LaNorris) Sellers, the amount of tackles that they break, and then they're on the next level, and then it's a first down. It's a big play over and over and over again. It happens very, very consistently. "Where's this game being played at? Williams-Brice Stadium. Space Odyssey. The rooster will be crowing very annoyingly. This feels like a trench war. This feels like LaNorris Sellers (having a big game). I told you before the season that South Carolina was going to get somebody. This is who they're gonna get. This is gonna be a great game, but I think it's the run game of South Carolina. It's breaking tackles and making extra plays." "What South Carolina can do through the passing game is create some explosive plays off of the run game, and because of that, they finally get their finish," added Pollack. "They finally finish the game strong and run out the clock with LaNorris Sellers and company in the run game. … South Carolina has some legitimate dudes on their squad. I think it's a good game, but I also think South Carolina is really talented, and that's a tough place to play. South Carolina wins by seven, 27-20." Tennessee and South Carolina will kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams
picks.blurb: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams John Adams, Knoxville News Sentinel Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:06 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia's Kirby Smart has won so much for so long that he's regarded as the best coach in college football . But after a last-second loss to Auburn, he proved he can also be one of the sport's best quotes. "Humility is a week away," he said. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel would be wise to paraphrase Smart's comment before the Vols take on South Carolina at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia. The Vols are coming off a dominant 26-10 victory over Alabama . They're 6-1 and on the cusp of the top 10. But all they gained from a victory over their archrival could be lost with a loss to the unranked Gamecocks. Tennessee 26, South Carolina 16: In an unpredictable SEC season, team performances have varied drastically from one Saturday to the next. Based on that trend, Tennessee could be next in line to take a tumble after a big win. But amid all the SEC's inconsistency, UT's defense has remained steadfast. Something else to consider: Tennessee has been coming on strong in the second half; in South Carolina's last five SEC games dating back to last season, it has lost leads of 27, 16 and 17 points. LSU 31, Auburn 23: While I believe Tennessee's defense will prevent a letdown against South Carolina, I'm not as confident about Auburn's chances for prosperity after upsetting No. 1 Georgia. The LSU offense hasn't always been the model of consistency, but neither has Auburn's. LSU's challenge: Winning on the road. It already has lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky. That's a carryover from the Brian Kelly era. The Tigers lost all four of their SEC road games in 2025. They also lost their last two conference road games in 2024. So, they will take an eight-game SEC road losing streak with them to Jordan-Hare Stadium. They're due. Alabama 30, Texas A&M 15: The Tide also are due for a win after losing back-to-back games against Georgia and Tennessee. They can be grateful that their schedule offers a home game against the three-loss Aggies, who have lost two SEC games by 21 or more points. Texas A&M's 41-0 victory over The Citadel hardly qualifies as the beginning of a turnaround. However, it at least demonstrated that the Aggies aren't devoid of young talent. Freshman running back KJ Edwards led Texas A&M with 116 yards rushing on 16 carries. Freshman wide receiver Aaron Gregory led the Aggies' injury-depleted receiving corps with six catches for 94 yards. Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 20: This matchup is all about quarterbacks. You can't be sure if Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor is healthy enough to play. Without him, Mississippi State lost 31-0 to LSU. With him, it scored 38 points against Minnesota and 41 on South Carolina. The health of Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't an issue. Performance is his problem. Mateer is a fiery competitor and a running threat. But he doesn't protect the football. He has lost two fumbles and thrown seven interceptions in six games. And he has thrown only two more touchdown passes than interceptions. In Mateer's last season at Washington State (2024), he threw seven interceptions in 12 games. He also threw 29 touchdown passes. Texas 30, Ole Miss 27: The Longhorns are getting less for their NIL money than any other program. But just because you have a big-bucks payroll doesn't mean you have a big-play offense. Texas has scored fewer than 24 points in four of its six games. ADAMS: Tennessee football should be well aware of South Carolina threat on road And the Longhorns are on the verge of playing themselves out of the playoffs for a second consecutive season. But they might be catching the Rebels at the right time. A week after beating LSU, Ole Miss lost to Florida by 28 points. Now, it's coming off a 28-point victory over Missouri. Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 23: You might conclude that after five consecutive victories, the Wildcats are about to learn, as Smart said, that "humility is a week away." As accurate as Smart's assessment might be in general, it doesn't apply if you're playing Vanderbilt. Record: 59-14 (.793), 48-26 (.642) against the spread. John Adams is a senior columnist. He may be reached at 865-342-6284 or john.adams@knoxnews.com. Published: Oct 22, 2026 · 10:00 AM EDT The Fearless Prediction had wavering confidence in Josh Heupel and the Tennessee Volunteers last week and could not have been more wrong. Tennessee's defense is absolutely legit, and the offense showed remarkable physical and mental toughness in a dominating 26-10 victory over Alabama . We won't doubt the Big Orange again. (Looks at schedule.) If you had to explain to a friend who knows nothing about college football what a “trap game” was, Tennessee's upcoming visit to South Carolina potentially fits the bill. The Vols do not play well at Williams-Brice. Tennessee's loss in 2016 put it on the road to losing the SEC East. The Vols' loss in 2022 probably cost them a spot in the 4-team College Football Playoff and saw their star QB Hendon Hooker rip up his knee, ending his college career. There's also the matter of Connor Stalions and how he may or may not have assisted South Carolina. College football rarely disappoints. In terms of this season, the Vols are coming off an impressive victory and a rivalry win, no less. Can they put that in the rearview? As for South Carolina, Shane Beamer is coaching for his job. Last time out, the Gamecocks pulled off a surprising win at Florida , and now are well rested following a bye week. Tennessee's defense is good. Really good. Following a 5-sack performance against Alabama, the Vols have 30 sacks on the season, tops in the FBS. They are also 6th in the country in tackles for loss with 58. Against the Crimson Tide, the Vols stopped 11 of 13 third-down attempts and allowed only 54 rushing yards. Defensive linemen Xavier Gilliam and Tyree Weathersby are the modern-day Undertaker and Kane, causing havoc with a combined 11.5 sacks and 18.5 tackles for loss. Linebackers Amare Campbell and Arion Carter are at the top of the tackle table with 46 and 43, respectively. The Vols have also collected 13 turnovers, tied for 10th-best in the FBS. New defensive coordinator Jim Knowles has been a revelation, leading one of the best groups in the country. As for that Tennessee offense, why don't they just build the whole plane out of DeSean Bishop? He's now averaging nearly 120 rushing yards per game with a healthy 6 yards per carry. Against Alabama, he had 159 rushing yards and 2 scores. Having Bishop takes a lot off the plate of redshirt freshman QB George MacIntyre, who seems to have cemented his place as Tennessee's starter. He'll get the call for his 2nd career road start on Saturday. As for South Carolina, the Gamecocks were left for dead a couple of weeks ago, as was their head coach, Shane Beamer. They had lost 3 straight, including a crushing OT loss to Kentucky . But then came a startling 38-19 victory over Florida. QB LaNorris Sellers has a combined 291.5 yards passing and rushing, with 14 combined TDs. South Carolina needs a big game from Sellers if it is going to win on Saturday. Tennessee doesn't give up many big plays, but needs to be aware of WR Nyck Harbor, averaging 16.4 yards per reception. RB Matt Fuller is gaining 81 yards per game on the ground. Defensively, senior LB Justin Okoronkwo leads the Gamecocks with 43 tackles. Lineman Tomiwa Durojaiye has 4.5 tackles for loss. If special teams are to be a factor, Tennessee's Cooper Ranvier has made 10 of 11 FGs, South Carolina's Malik Orsan has made 8 of 10 FGs. Weird things happen in this game, especially when played in Columbia. But Tennessee gets a break with an afternoon kickoff. That means less time for those Gamecocks fans to pregame. It's not revenge the Vols are after on Saturday… it's the reckoning. Four years ago, South Carolina fans reveled in destroying Tennessee's Playoff dreams. They won't get a repeat performance. Fearless Prediction: Tennessee 26, South Carolina 17 Mark Nagi has covered Tennessee athletics for over 20 years. He is the author of “Decade of Dysfunction,” an in-depth look at all that led to the crazy coaching search of 2017 at Tennessee. The book is available on Amazon. By Parker Gillam Published: Oct 21, 2026 · 7:58 PM EDT Tennessee is set to pay a visit to South Carolina this Saturday, and the Volunteers are still riding high following their upset win over Alabama last weekend. But Columbia has been far from kind to the Volunteers in recent memory, as they've dropped 6 of their last 8 contests at Williams-Brice Stadium heading into this one. picks.headline: Can Tennessee football maintain momentum at South Carolina? Our pick
picks.blurb: News Sports Business Go Knoxville Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Can Tennessee football maintain momentum at South Carolina? Our pick Emmett Siegel Knoxville News Sentinel Oct. 22, 2026, 5:07 a.m. ET The No. 11 Tennessee Volunteers will face the South Carolina Gamecocks on October 24. South Carolina is looking to build on a recent win against Florida after a slow start to their season. Key players for the Gamecocks include quarterback LaNorris Sellers and edge rusher Dylan Stewart. Tennessee's defense has been dominant this season, leading the SEC in several key statistical categories. Tennessee football is tasked with avoiding a letdown after a convincing win against Alabama, and it'll have to do so in a hostile road environment. The No. 11 Vols (6-1, 3-1 SEC) play South Carolina (3-3, 1-3) at Williams-Brice Stadium on Oct. 24 (3:30 p.m., ESPN). Tennessee's last trip to Columbia in 2022 ended with a blowout loss that knocked it out of College Football Playoff contention. It'll try to avoid a similar fate this year and maintain its footing in the CFP race before its open week. Here's what to know about the matchup. South Carolina's season started slow before Florida win Just a few weeks ago, it looked as though South Carolina's season was hanging on by a thread. The Gamecocks started 0-3 in SEC play. After a 4-8 season last year, coach Shane Beamer's seat was getting scorching hot. But they bought themselves a bit more time with a 38-19 win at Florida before the open week. And while the game before that was a home loss to Kentucky, South Carolina was one two-point conversion stop away from winning in overtime. Beamer still needs a decent finish to quiet discussions about his job security, but his team has shown it is capable of beating just about anyone in the SEC. In 2024, with many of the same key players, the Gamecocks went 9-4 and nearly made the CFP. LaNorris Sellers, Dylan Stewart star at premium positions South Carolina has game changers at premium positions on both offense and defense with quarterback LaNorris Sellers and edge rusher Dylan Stewart. When Sellers is on his game he is one of the best quarterbacks in the SEC, but he's been glaringly inconsistent. He had turnover problems in losses to Alabama and Mississippi State and was at that point tied for the second-worst completion rate in the SEC (62.1%). The next week he threw for 226 yards and two touchdowns with 147 rushing yards against Kentucky. Stewart has also had a season of ups and downs. He is a likely top-10 pick the 2027 NFL Draft but missed three of the first five games of this season, one because of a suspension after he punched an Alabama player in the helmet. Then he came back against Florida and dominated with two forced fumbles and a sack. If Sellers and Stewart are at their best, South Carolina can beat any team it plays. Tennessee's defense has been elite Few defenses in the country are as well-equipped as Tennessee's to handle a mobile quarterback like Sellers. The Vols rank first in the SEC in sacks, explosive plays allowed, tackles for loss, scoring defense, opposing passer rating and fourth-down defense. Defensive coordinator Jim Knowles' unit has been nothing short of dominant through seven games. The Vols have also forced multiple turnovers in three of their last four games, including four against Alabama. South Carolina lost the turnover battle in its first three SEC games and lost them all. When it was plus-three against Florida, it won by multiple scores. Tennessee vs South Carolina prediction Tennessee 24, South Carolina 21: This is a major trap game for Tennessee on the road after an emotional win, but its defense should travel just fine. The matchup may be decided by who's better between Vols running back DeSean Bishop and the Gamecocks' run defense that ranks third in the SEC. Oddsmakers slightly favor South Carolina in a spot that feels ripe for an unranked-over-ranked result. Still, picking against Tennessee's defense has been a fool's errand. picks.headline: ESPN predicts the winner of Clemson football vs. Virginia Tech
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the Hokies into Memorial Stadium, less than a year after he squared off against the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl at Yankee Stadium while playing for Penn State. In that game, Grunkemeyer threw for 260 yards and two touchdowns in Penn State's 22-10 win over Clemson. A third-year QB who committed to the Nittany Lions and James Franklin, Grunkemeyer followed his former Penn State coach to Blacksburg after Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech last November after the Nittany Lions parted ways with the 12-year skipper barely a month earlier. He has thrown for 1,984 yards and 15 touchdowns to two interceptions through seven games this season. Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech lead the ACC in passing yards , though the Hokies have played one more game than Darian Mensah and the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Clemson's passing game has been a complete contrast, to say the least. Through their first six contests, the Tigers have thrown a combined two touchdown psases between Week 1 starter Christopher Vizzina and former four-star freshman Tait Reynolds. The Tigers are second to last in the ACC in total offense with 340.7 yards per game while Virginia Tech ranks sixth (449.7) in the conference. Reynolds was 17 of 26 for 127 yards in Clemson's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern in Week 6. He has thrown for 943 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions entering his fifth start of 2026. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Clemson as a 2.5-point favorite over Virginia Tech, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, gives Clemson a 55.9% chance to win. Virginia Tech has a 44.1% chance. The Tigers are No. 48 in ESPN's FPI with a 6.5 rating, which ranks 10th among ACC teams. Virginia Tech has a 6.6 rating that's one spot ahead of Clemson in ESPN's metrics. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Oregon State (6.0) in the FPI. Clemson football has longshot odds of reaching ACC title game entering Week 8 In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 88.4%. The Tigers' chances of winning the ACC, however, are just 0.3%. That's down from 0.9% before the Tigers' 41-13 loss to the Miami Hurricanes on Oct. 3. Clemson's chances of reaching the 12-team College Football Playoff are 1.5%, which is down from 4.1% prior to the Miami loss and down from 22.2% entering the season. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.1 rating on offense (No. 98 nationally, down one spot from last week) and a 19.5 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is up five spots from before the Tigers' win over Charleston Southern. What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. Virginia Tech has scored at least 20 points in every game this season, and Clemson has a stout defense. However, you have to think that Virginia Tech finds a way to break the 20-point plateau. It might not seem like a bit of a bold prediction, but the way the Tigers play defense and being on the road under the lights at Memorial Stadium, it is. If they want to have a shot at pulling off the upset, they will have to. Clemson's offense has sputtered at times this season, and getting off the field with some turnovers would go a long way toward securing an upset on the road. Turnovers both ways are going to play a big part in the outcome. Luke Reynolds records another 100 yards plus receiving Clemson coach Dabo Swinney spoke this week about Hokies tight end Luke Reynolds and how good he is. He got an up-close look at him last season in the Pinstripe Bowl when Penn State defeated the Tigers at Yankee Stadium. away.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. The Hokies' contest against the Tigers is set for Saturday, Oct. 24, at 7 p.m. ET in Clemso

away.headline: Final Injury Report for Georgia Tech vs Virginia Tech: Who's in and Who's out for the Yellow Jackets?
away.blurb: The Yellow Jackets are going to be trying to pull off an upset against the Hokies today, but they are going to have to do so with some key players out. The final availability report is out for this game, and it includes the final status for running back Justice Haynes, who was listed as doubtful coming into Saturday, as well as offensive lineman Josh Petty and defensive lineman Landen Marshall. RB Justice Haynes and OT Josh Petty are going to be game-time decisions. If Haynes is unable to go today, Trelain Maddox and Chad Alexander would be the top options in the backfield for the Yellow Jackets today against Virginia Tech. Maddox is coming off the best game of his career last week against Duke. Riggs, the Yellow Jackets starting center, came back from an injury last week in the win over Duke, but was hurt during the game and did not return. He was not on the injury report this week and should be starting in the middle of the Yellow Jackets offensive line against what has been one of the ACC's best defensive fronts through the first part of the season. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/georgiatech as Final Injury Report for Georgia Tech vs Virginia Tech: Who's in and Who's out for the Yellow Jackets? . Kickoff time is getting closer for Georgia Tech and Virginia Tech. How do these injuries impact Georgia Tech today? There are two notable names not on the injury report this week and those are Jameson Riggs and Noah Carter. Carter has been perhaps the Yellow Jackets' most consistent pass rusher (although the pass rush has not been very good), and without Walker, Boyd, or Hoffler to get after the quarterback, Carter is going to be relied on to put pressure on Hokies QB Ethan Grunkemeyer, and Virginia Tech's offensive line has not been one of the best in the ACC so far this season. As poorly as the season started for Georgia Tech, a win on the road against the Hokies would be something that could potentially start to turn their season around. The Yellow Jackets have only one conference loss and with the ACC looking wide open after Miami, Georgia Tech can star to build some momentum that could get them to their fourth consecutive bowl appearance under Brent Key. away.blurb: News Sports Business Entertainment Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL ACC injury report for Clemson vs. Virginia Tech: Who is out? Drew Landon Clemson Wire Oct. 22, 2026, 6:30 a.m. CT Clemson football's initial availability report carries 10 injuries, one being fresh. Freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is the only newly announced absence ahead of Saturday night’s game against Virginia Tech, while most of the remaining names have been unavailable for weeks. Sellars suffered a concussion and entered protocol following what Dabo Swinney described as the freshman’s best practice of the season. Clemson will hold him out when the Tigers host the Hokies at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound receiver had finally worked his way back from the hamstring issue that limited him during fall camp. Swinney said Sellars made two impressive catches during practice and had established himself as Clemson’s fourth receiver behind Bryant Wesco Jr., Tyler Brown and T.J. Moore. Virginia Tech has its own problems up front. Offensive lineman Justin Terry is out, while Nathaniel Wright, Lucas Austin, and Montavious Cunningham are questionable. The Hokies allowed seven sacks in last week’s 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech . Sellars has only three catches for eight yards this season, so Clemson is not losing a premium part of its passing game. His absence still shortens a receiver rotation that is already missing Cole Turner and reserve Chase Byrd. Turner has been away from the program since fall camp while handling a personal matter There is some good health news from the report. Running back Jay Haynes returned against Charleston Southern for his first game action since suffering multiple knee injuries in the 2024 ACC Championship Game. Defensive tackle Kourtney Kelly also made his Clemson debut after tearing his ACL during spring practice.
