Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Virginia Tech Week 8 Availability Report: Latest Updates Ahead of Clemson Matchup Skip to main content SI.COM More from Virginia Tech Hokies On SI FOOTBALL Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: WR Shamarius "Snook" Peterkin Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemso

home.headline: Clemson True Freshman WR Gordon Sellars III Ruled Out vs. Virginia Tech
home.blurb: Clemson True Freshman WR Gordon Sellars III Ruled Out vs. Virginia Tech - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Clemson True Freshman WR Gordon Sellars III Ruled Out vs. Virginia Tech Clemson true freshman WR Gordon Sellars III has been ruled out for this week's contest vs. Virginia Tech due to a concussion. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Angelo Feliberty Thu, October 22, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads "Well, he had his best day yesterday, but he's gonna be out this weekend," he said. "He's got a concussion, so he'll be out unfortunately. But he had a great day; had a couple of good catches." "I thought, Gordo was a guy that came out of spring ball that I thought, 'Here we go,' and he dealt with some injuries in fall camp, and it kind of set him back," Morris said on Wednesday. "It was really good to see his speed. I thought he flashed." "You know, he's really kind of been that next guy, and that's really been since the spring," he finished. "He just kind of emerged, and then he pulled his hamstring in camp and has kind of been limited a good bit, but has been able to play some and kind of been working his way back." As it stands, there's no clear timetable for Sellars' return, but true freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds will still have plenty of weapons in the Week 8 conference matchup, with Bryant Wesco Jr. and T.J. Moore ready to get back on track. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/clemson as Clemson True Freshman WR Gordon Sellars III Ruled Out vs. Virginia Tech . Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut As the Clemson Tigers head back into ACC play against Virginia Tech this weekend, they'll be without a key depth piece on the offensive side of the ball. Speaking during media availability on Wednesday, head coach Dabo Swinney announced that true freshman wideout Gordon Sellars III will miss the Week 8 contest vs. the Hokies due to a concussion he suffered in practice on Tuesday. As we reported earlier this season, Sellars has been a standout , not just among the freshmen but among the receivers as a whole, taking over as the primary backup on the outside while sophomore Juju Preston fills the backup slot role. It's an untimely setback for a freshman who has been trending up, and one that offensive coordinator Chad Morris says he saw coming back during the spring period. Swinney shared a similar view, and the concussion is especially frustrating for a young talent who worked hard to come back from the hamstring injury Morris referenced during fall camp. Not to mention, junior tight end Christian Bentancur is coming off a career-high four catches for 74 yards against Charleston Southern in Week 7. So we'll see if Morris continues to open up the playbook for pass-catching outside of receivers. Swinney and the Tigers are set to kick off from Memorial Stadium at 7 p.m. ET,

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Texas is looking to end a two-game skid and get its College Football Playoff hopes back on track against an Ole Miss team coming off its best performance of the year so far Getty Images Arch Manning grew up with Ole Miss all around him. His uncle Eli's jersey was retired in Oxford, and so was his grandfather Archie's No. 18. On Saturday night, Arch faces the Rebels for the first time, possibly at the lowest point of his career. Questions have swirled around Arch during a two-game losing streak that has the Longhorns on the brink of falling completely out of the polls after rising to No. 1 in September with a comeback win against top-ranked Ohio State . He threw two interceptions, including a pick-six, in the loss to Oklahoma , and last week he lost a fumble on a strip sack with two minutes remaining, allowing Florida to hold on for a win, Manning's first home loss as a starter. Afterward, Sarkisian said he would evaluate the offense, including Manning's role in the offense. Now Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) is trying to avoid joining 1965 Texas and 1957 Texas A&M as the only teams to lose three straight games in a season after entering as the AP No. 1 team. The Longhorns will be without the nation's sacks leader, Colin Simmons , who has a high ankle sprain. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) has won two straight by a combined 63 points and has redisovered its groove following a 28-point win against nationally-ranked Missouri last week. Ole Miss vs. Texas: Need to know Arch Manning's evaluation : Manning is expected to start Saturday, but how short will the leash be? Backup KJ Lacey has gotten more first-team reps over the last two weeks, fueling speculation he could step in against the Rebels. Manning threw only seven interceptions in 13 games last season. He's up to five picks through six starts this season. "He's our starter, but I need to see a better version of Arch Manning like I need to see a better version of a lot of guys on our offensive football team right now, but we need to see a better version of him this week," Sarkisian said. Life without Colin Simmons : Simmons leads the FBS with 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss. He had eight tackles, four TFL and a sack against Florida before he was carted off in the fourth quarter, and reports have him out three to four weeks. That's a problem against Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who has thrown a touchdown pass in 19 straight games, tied for the second-longest streak in Ole Miss history. His 20 total touchdowns rank second in the SEC, and Ole Miss leads the FBS in red zone touchdown percentage (87.5%). Ole Miss rebuilt itself after Florida : The Rebels left Gainesville in September after a 52-28 loss Golding called an "old-fashioned butt whooping." The Gators ran for 302 yards, and Ole Miss managed one tackle for loss and no sacks. Since a bye week, Ole Miss beat Vanderbilt 52-17 on the road and Missouri 31-3 at home. Kewan Lacy (122 yards) and Makhi Frazier (101) both topped 100 yards against the Tigers. The road remains the question. Ole Miss is 1-10 in its last 11 road games against ranked SEC teams, and Golding's lone road game as head coach against a ranked opponent was the loss at No. 21 Florida. Kewan Lacy comes home : Lacy grew up in Dallas as a Texas fan, and dreamed of playing for the Longhorns, but they never offered the running back a scholarship. "I can't wait to see them," Lacy said this offseason. He has 29 career rushing touchdowns, third in school history and the most in the SEC since 2025, though Golding has managed his workload since he missed the Florida game. His 13-game rushing touchdown streak ended against Missouri, but he still ran for a season-high 122 yards. Where to watch Ole Miss vs. Texas live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium -- Austin, Texas TV : ABC | Live stream : Fubo ( try free ) Ole Miss vs. Texas: prediction, picks Texas is a 2.5-point favorite, and the SportsLine model projects a 29-17 Longhorns win. History backs it. Ole Miss is 1-6 straight up and against the spread as a road underdog against ranked teams since 2020, and Texas has won three straight home games against top-10 opponents. But is this the same Texas team that has been so successful at home? The Longhorns scored 17 points against a Florida defense that ranked last in the SEC, and the Gators sacked Manning five times with 11 tackles for loss. Texas hasn't scored more than 24 points against a power opponent. The offensive line is a mess, ranking 111th in sacks allowed, and the running game is subpar at 101st. The Longhorns are also 1-5 against the spread this season and haven't covered five straight. Ole Miss has the better quarterback and a run game that just went for 257 yards. Without Simmons, Texas loses the one defender built to wreck Chambliss' night. Texas also lacks championship-level coaching. against Ole Miss. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Arch Manning (16) leads Texas against Ole Miss and Trinidad Chambliss (6). For the first time in over a decade, Texas and Ole Miss meet on Saturday at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas, at 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The Longhorns are 3.5-point home favorites, and despite back-to-back losses, my Ole Miss vs. Texas prediction and college football picks project Arch Manning to pull off a win against his namesake's alma mater. TOP PICK Who will win Ole Miss vs Texas: Texas -3.5 Archie Manning never played against Texas, but Arch Manning has the chance to lead the Longhorns to their first win against his grandfather and uncle's alma mater since 2012. It's a good time to buy low on a Texas team I would take to cover up to -5.5 at home against Ole Miss . While the Longhorns have lost two straight, they still have the clear defensive advantage, even with Colin Simmons unlikely to play. The Texas defense ranks sixth nationally in available yards percentage (31.2%) and 14th in havoc rate (20%). Meanwhile, the Ole Miss defense struggled in ranked matchups away from home, allowing 90 points across two games. It's a big ask for Trinidad Chambliss to make up for his own defense again against one of the top defenses in the country. Chambliss is coming off arguably his worst game of the season, too (80.4 QBR, 65.7% adjusted completion percentage vs. Missouri ). Ole Miss vs Texas Over/Under pick: Over 53.5 While Texas' defensive advantage should make the difference in a Longhorns win, I'm expecting enough points to be scored for the Over to hit at 54.5 or better . The Ole Miss defense ranks 65th nationally in success rate (43.5%) and 89th in net EPA per drive, while allowing the most yards per game in the SEC (390). It's been at its worst away from home, allowing 35.6 points per game outside Oxford , helping the Over in all three of those games. But the Rebels have arguably the best QB in the country in Chambliss, who ranks top 20 in QBR (83.4) and TD passes (14). He and Kewan Lacy should move Ole Miss' offense with enough consistency for the Over to hit. I like Texas to win 31-24. Ole Miss vs Texas combo This is the No. 2 must-watch game in my Top 25 predictions for Week 8, with Manning and Sarkisian looking for redemption and needing to cool down their seats. While Chambliss is my midseason first-team All-American QB, Ole Miss can't keep getting away with relying on him to carry it to wins... allowing 29.2 points per game against ranked teams will catch up to the Rebels. Without Simmons, this Texas defense will take a step back, but not a big enough step for Ole Miss to light it up and make up for its own defensive woes. Games away from home have been unkind to the Rebels, especially their defense, and I think Maning, Sarkisian, and the Longhorns offense will rise to the occasion to take advantage. picks.headline: “They’re Going to Condense”: Former UCLA HC Predicts Trouble for Texas vs Ole Miss as Arch Manning’s Issues are Set to Force Tactical Switch
picks.blurb: “They’re Going to Condense”: Former UCLA HC Predicts Trouble for Texas vs Ole Miss as Arch Manning’s Issues are Set to Force Tactical Switch - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning warms up before a game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. © Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Prateek Singh Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:41 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Arch Manning's struggles against the Florida Gators have put the Texas Longhorns in a difficult position ahead of their matchup against the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday. Manning threw for 173 yards, completed 14 of 20 passes, and threw one touchdown. According to former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel, Texas will need to make key adjustments to its strategy ahead of the upcoming game. During an appearance on CBS Sports, Neuheisel picked Ole Miss to win. "I'm concerned for Texas in this game, not because I don't think they'll play hard and be geared up to play their best game of the season, but I feel like because of all the pressure on Arch, they're going to condense, and condensing will not be the answer to going against Pete Golding defense," he said . Neuheisel pointed out that Arch Manning attempted just 20 passes against Florida, arguing that such an approach will not be effective against the Ole Miss Rebels. While the Texas Longhorns have won four of their six games this season, Manning has shown only flashes of brilliance rather than the consistency expected of him. Overall, Manning has completed 106 of 166 passes for 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns, and five interceptions. After his performance against the Gators, speculation began that he could be benched for the upcoming game. However, head coach Steve Sarkisian made it clear that Arch Manning will remain the team's starting quarterback. "There's no doubt about it, Arch can play better for us, but he's our starter," he said , per Fox Sports. "We need to see a better version of him this week." Sarkisian said Manning is a quality player and that, as a coach, it is his job to bring out the best in him on the field. Former Texas Coach Heaps Praise on Arch Manning On an episode of THE STAMPEDE, former Texas coach Mack Brown said Arch Manning and the rest of the Longhorns are playing under immense pressure. He believes the team needs to free itself from that pressure before stepping onto the field. In Brown's view, Manning has the talent and ability to help get Texas back on track. "Arch's gotta go back and be the Arch we saw at the last of last year," he said. "He's good enough, he's athletic enough, he's smart enough, and for a 22-year-old, he has handled this pressure so well." Brown said the upcoming matchup against the Ole Miss Rebels will be crucial for the Longhorns and could shape their chances of making the College Football Playoff this season. Badgers Bounce Back? Klatt's Week 8 CFB Picks Updated Oct. 22, 2026 2:53 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Upsets, a top-25 shuffle and a new No. 1 headlined a chaotic Week 7 of college football. Are we in for more of the same in Week 8? It starts with No. 7 Ole Miss heading to No. 19 Texas. After suffering its second straight loss to unranked opponents – Oklahoma in Week 6 and Florida in Week 7 – all eyes are on Texas to see if Arch Manning will pull off a bounce-back win. Another conference showdown to watch is No. 14 Houston at No. 10 Utah, with both coming off Week 7 wins: Houston's Conner Weigman threw five total touchdowns, and Utah narrowly escaped Colorado with a 27-24 victory. This top-15 matchup will carry major conference championship implications. What does FOX Sports' Joel Klatt think of the Week 8 slate? Here are his Week 8 picks and previews, revealed on the latest episode of "The Joel Klatt Show". Ole Miss 28, Texas 21 Ole Miss sits 5-1 on the season heading into a road contest at No. 19 Texas. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) Spread: Texas -3.5 Moneyline: Texas -162, Ole Miss +136 Klatt's thoughts: "Ole Miss, after blowing out Missouri, they go to Texas. And now Texas has to play at home off of back-to-back losses. Two straight for Steve Sarkisian and the boys. Based on the film that I watched, this entire offense has got to get better. It is not just Arch Manning, that is a fallacy. You cannot just replace Arch Manning and fix the Texas offense. That is not in the equation. It's just not. The main culprit is their offensive line. Their offensive line is playing really poorly. So you need to simplify and allow them to come off the ball, allow them to run a few concepts, and do that well. If you're able to do that, I think that you can start to fix the offensive line. If you start to fix the offensive line, maybe you should start to fix the run game. If you start to fix the run, fix the run game, maybe Arch has more opportunities to throw the football. "I thought Ole Miss was going to be an average defense at one point. They shut down Missouri cold. [Missouri] couldn't do anything on the ground. Ole Miss dominated them on the ground. You still have Trinidad Chambliss. I still might take him No. 1 overall from a quarterback perspective. Running back Kewan Lacy is healthy. Their defense is right. Their star players are back, and as good as Texas' defense is they did struggle in the second half. They, as Sarkisian put it, kind of bled out and couldn't get a stop as DE Colin Simmons left that game with an injury. It's unclear whether he's going to return. Even if he does, he left on a cart. I can't imagine that he would be 100% even if he is on the football field. And now you've got to run around and defend Trinidad Chambliss? I don't love that at all. "I think Ole Miss wins this outright, 28-21. I'll take the -3.5 and take Ole Miss." Klatt's straight-up pick: Ole Miss Klatt's pick against the spread: Ole Miss +3.5 Utah 30, Houston 27 Devon Dampier and Utah pulled out a close 27-24 win over Colorado in Week 7. (Photo by Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Spread: Utah -6.5 Moneyline: Utah -225, Houston +185 Klatt's thoughts: "Houston at Utah. How about an underrated Houston win last week. Houston with a great performance, particularly out of their quarterback, Conner Weigman. They beat Drew Mestemaker and the Cowboys 35-32 in a great game. You know how I feel about Mestemaker. I think he's one of the better quarterbacks in the country. Houston's for real. I know that they lost that game earlier this year [against Texas Tech]. But man, they can throw the football, their defense can stop the run. Weigman is having a great season, he's second in the country in touchdown passes and total touchdowns. He's playing at a very high level. They've got two wide receivers that I like a lot, Amare Thomas and Trent Walker ... Now [Houston] has to go on the road and face Utah, who is historically very good at home in Salt Lake. I don't love how Houston played on the road against Colorado. "I didn't love what I saw from Utah. They faced a lot of lower-level competition, both from Power Four and otherwise to start, and they were hammering lower-end opponents. Then they face a few opponents with a pulse, like mid-Kansas and Colorado. They end up getting the wins, but in both of those games it's in doubt in the second half. As much as you know, I love Utah, I didn't even have them in my top 10. They still have Devon Dampier, they still have Wayshawn Parker. They should still be able to run the ball. But, Houston can stop the run. I think Utah could struggle to stop some of the run game against Conner Weigman and these two wide receivers. I see a bit of a higher scoring game. "I see Utah ultimately winning because of the home field. But I have to take the 6.5 towards Houston in this one. Utah wins it 31-27." Klatt's straight-up pick: Utah Klatt's pick against the spread: Houston +6.5 LSU 34, Auburn 30 Can LSU and Lane Kiffin avoid a road loss this season in its Week 8 showdown at Auburn? (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) Spread: LSU -7.5 Moneyline: LSU -298, Auburn +240 Klatt's thoughts: "LSU at Auburn. LSU is favored by 7.5 Auburn coming off of that huge win over Georgia. LSU routed Mississippi State 31-0. Remember, Mississippi State was without Kamario Taylor in that game, he was banged up, didn't play. At Auburn, I think you've got to look at LSU on the road and what they have been not only this year but in the recent past. LSU struggles on the road. They're 0-2 this year on the road. So, that needs to change for Lane Kiffin. Their defense needs to play well, obviously, because Byrum Brown has back-to-back 100-yard rushing games from the quarterback position, and that is the formula for Alex Golesh and Brown. "Like, I don't think Auburn is just going to get stomped out by LSU. They both have two losses, and 7.5 on the road is too much, not for a team that has lost their last six on the road. Now, I think LSU gets the win, but that's too many, so I've got to take the 7.5. I think LSU wins this 34-30. I'm going to take the 7.5 for Auburn. "I know it's an emotional win, and we have seen teams this year after emotional wins really have a letdown. I'm going to bank on the fact that [Auburn is] returning home and getting to play at home, and LSU's got to go on the road. I'm banking that Golesh is going to get Brown going on the edge a little bit. We'll see if LSU's defense can react. LSU is banged up. Lane Kiffin's lamenting the [nine-game conference schedule]. He's trying to throw excuses in front of his team." Klatt's straight-up pick: LSU Klatt's pick against the spread: Auburn +7.5 USC 24, Wisconsin 20 Jayden Maiava currently leads the Big Ten in passing yards with 2,045. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Spread: USC -2.5 Moneyline: USC -155, Wisconsin +130 Klatt's thoughts: "USC at Wisconsin. USC favored by 2.5 on the road, coming off of a bye week. Their last matchup was on the road against Penn State in the whiteout. Wisconsin was on the road last week in L.A., getting beat by UCLA in a 17-7 game. I'm really interested to see what that Penn State win did for USC. Their confidence on the road, their overall operation on the road. We have seen them struggle mightily, in particular going east. Even this year when they tried to go out to Rutgers, they got the win but it was sloppy, in particular on the defensive side. Then they go out there and they get the win over Penn State. And Wisconsin was able to beat Penn State also at Penn State. I think this could be a close game. "[USC has] got Trent Mosley back on the outside. They're getting a little healthier after the bye week. I just think that even if you're playing great defense, they're still going to score 21, 24 points. They should be able to run football a little bit. Wisconsin's not great against the run; they're okay, but not great against the run. I like what Luke Fickell has done. I am a big fan of this Wisconsin team, but they can't throw the football. Colton Joseph is a good, solid running quarterback, but they cannot throw the football. If that's the floor for USC, the only way Wisconsin gets there is if USC props them up. So Jayden Maiava's got to play clean. They can't turn the football over. You can't have special teams gaffes. And if they can play clean from a penalty perspective, I know that's a huge if, huge if. I think USC is able to go out there and get the win on the road, even in a close game, and even in a close win. "You've got to have them covering the 2.5. USC, 24-20 in this ball game." Klatt's straight-up pick: USC Klatt's pick against the spread: USC -2.5 Iowa 24, Minnesota 17 Jeremy Hecklinski led the Hawkeyes to a 41-24 win over Washington in his first start for Iowa. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Spread: Iowa -6.5 Moneyline: Iowa -258, Minnesota +210 Klatt's thoughts: "Iowa at Minnesota. Iowa is ranked 15th, they're favored by 6.5. They're playing really well. They blew out Washington and Seattle the last time we saw them play. I like Minnesota. I love P.J. Fleck . How are they scoring 17 against Iowa in this game? I don't see it. Meanwhile, they're not stopping the run. Purdue ran for over 300 yards on the ground against Minnesota last week. Don't love that aspect of what's going on. "So here we are with Iowa. They're going to run the football. They're going to play great defense. They're Iowa. I actually like Jeremy Hecklinski at quarterback, maybe even over Hank Brown. Their only loss was against Ohio State in a game in which Jeremiah Smith was going off and nobody on the planet could defend him. I think this is a team that's going to be there in the end in the Big Ten. You look at their schedule: it is manageable. I like Reece Vander Zee, their wide receiver. I like Hecklinski. I like their tight end. Their defense is always good, and again, that rush defense from Minnesota just scares me. After Purdue was able to get after them on the ground, maybe the defense against Michigan was more about Michigan than it was against Minnesota. "I'm going to go Iowa in this one. I think that they cover the 6.5, even on the road, something along the lines of, you know 24-17." away.headline: Texas releases injury report for Ole Miss matchup
away.blurb: Texas star edge Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for Saturday’s matchup after sustaining a high ankle sprain in the loss to Florida, while running back Hollywood Smothers is listed as questionable. Smothers reportedly missed practice on Monday due to a shoulder injury. Other names listed for the Longhorns are wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman (both questionable), as well as freshman edge Richard Wesley (out). away.headline: Three Ole Miss offensive linemen on injury report, but there’s reason for optimism
away.blurb: Ole Miss has some personnel questions heading into Saturday night's showdown at Texas, but one part of Wednesday's SEC availability report stood out more than anything else. Three starting offensive linemen appeared on it. Starting left tackle Terez Davis and center Brycen Sanders were listed as questionable, while right guard Patrick Kutas was listed as probable. The good news for Ole Miss is there's no reason to believe any of the three are in serious danger of missing the game. Kutas, especially, would be a surprise absence given his probable designation. Sanders returned to last week's 31-3 win over Missouri after leaving with an injury, and while Davis didn't come back, he remained on the sideline in uniform. Still, it's hard to ignore seeing three starters from the same position group show up on the report before a road trip to Austin. The concern isn't necessarily whether they'll play. It's the fact Ole Miss is entering one of its biggest games of the season with questions along the offensive front. As for Kewan Lacy, his inclusion feels far less significant. Lacy was listed as probable after briefly leaving last week's game with a hamstring issue, but he still ran for 122 yards against Missouri. At this point, it wouldn't be surprising if his name appears on most injury reports the rest of the season as Ole Miss manages the situation. The bigger story remains the offensive line. If the Rebels have all three starters available Saturday night, they'll likely feel good about where they stand. But heading into a hostile road environment against a talented Texas defense, it's a group worth monitoring. Colin Simmons' absence would be a big break for Ole Miss While Ole Miss is watching the health of its offensive line, Texas appears likely to be without one of the nation's premier pass rushers. EDGE Colin Simmons was listed as doubtful after suffering an ankle sprain in last week's loss to Florida. That designation aligns with reports earlier this week indicating Simmons is expected to miss multiple weeks. Barring a surprising turnaround, it would be unexpected to see him on the field Saturday. That's significant for Ole Miss. Simmons leads the nation with 10.5 sacks and has been the centerpiece of the Texas pass rush. The Longhorns also listed EDGE Richard Wesley as out, further impacting their depth up front. Texas still has plenty of defensive talent, so this isn't a matchup-changing development by itself. But for an Ole Miss offensive line dealing with multiple injury concerns, potentially avoiding the nation's leading sacker is about as favorable a piece of injury news as the Rebels could have received this week. away.headline: Colin Simmons ruled doubtful for Ole Miss game in first Texas injury report
away.blurb: Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for the upcoming SEC contest at Royal-Memorial Stadium. Simmons exited last week's 27-24 loss to the Florida Gators early in the fourth quarter due to a right-leg injury, and he did not return to the game. Simmons will look to continue his climb up two all-time Texas leaderboards upon his potential return to the field this week/later this season. Simmons raised his career sack total to 31 1/2 in the loss to Florida, moving him to No. 3 on Texas' all-time leaderboard (and nine sacks behind Kiki DeAyala's program-record 40.5 sacks). Simmons also has DeAyala's single-season record in his sights. Simmons exited the weekend with 10 1/2 sacks in 2026, 12 sacks behind DeAyala's record-setting 22 1/2-sack season in 1982. Texas will face perhaps college football's best quarterback Saturday when Ole Miss ' Trinidad Chambliss comes to Austin. The Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) will likely do so without their best defensive player. This video created with the assistance of AI. Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said Saturday he believed Simmons suffered a right-knee injury against Florida, but was unaware of the injury's severity. Sarkisian didn't elaborate on Simmons' injury Monday, but Orangeblood's Anwar Richardson reported Simmons will miss three-to-four weeks due to a high-ankle sprain. Simmons' exit against Florida halted his statistical climb and hindered the Longhorns defense. Texas will likely now be without Simmons against Ole Miss and Chambliss, a scary situation after back-to-back SEC losses. Read this story on statesman.com

picks.headline: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 4:14 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will host Vanderbilt under the lights at Kroger Field on Saturday night, as it is the final game before the Wildcats enter a much needed bye week. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen in two weeks after the Wildcats bye week, and there is a great chance we see Kentucky on the graphic if they can improve to 7-1 against Vanderbilt. There shouldn't be any extra motivation needed, as a lot of these players remember the beatdown that happened in Nashville last season when Vanderbilt defeated Kentucky 45-17 in a blowout fashion. Kentucky has an opportunity to return the favor on Saturday, as the Commodores have one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Vanderbilt is struggling in a lot of ways on the defensive side of the football, and Kentucky's offense should be able to capitalize. The Commodores rank last in the SEC in pressure rate and tackle for loss rate, they have had a difficult time of forcing negative plays. Vanderbilt also allows the highest success rate in conference, and Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in offensive success rate. The real key to watch in my opinion is early down conversion rate and third down conversion rate, Vanderbilt's defense allows the highest percentage to opponents in the SEC; Kentucky's offense is one of the best in the country at converting on early downs and they have a chance to improve on third downs this weekend. There are a few players to watch on Vanderbilt's defense, and we will get more into that when we release our X factors for the game. It starts up front with veteran edge defender Miles Capers and defensive tackle Issa Ouattara who is a massive 6'7, 305-pound lineman that clogs up the middle. On the back end, senior safety CJ Heard is a player who plays in the box and can make plays all over the field; Heard is dangerous as a blitzer, he is a sure tackler and is probably the best player on the team in coverage. However, there is a stark contrast in this defense compared to the one the Wildcats just faced in Oklahoma. Vanderbilt has allowed 121 total points in their last three games against Georgia, Ole Miss and Arkansas. The Commodores are allowing 40 points per game over the last three weeks. This is probably the worst defense left on Kentucky's schedule. This creates a perfect opportunity for the Wildcats to get things going offensively to improve to 7-1 heading into the bye week. Vanderbilt has the lowest pressure and tackle for loss rate in the SEC, as previously mentioned, so this is a game where all eyes are on the Kentucky offensive line. This is a game they should dominate, they can get movement in the running game and keep Minchey clean for 60 minutes. Vanderbilt is allowing over four yards per carry and 146 rushing yards per game. You have to wonder if the coaching staff keeps CJ Baxter out of this game to get him to the bye week so he is as close to 100% as possible for the final stretch; this could be another heavy Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes game. Kentucky has yet to put together four quarters of football where they are firing on all cylinders. I think this is the game we could see that play out, specifically from an offensive standpoint. Now that the Wildcats are in the thick of the College Football Playoff hunt, how you win in these games can matter to a degree. Kentucky needs a dominant win on Saturday to keep that momentum going into the bye week. picks.headline: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 6:38 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will try to keep to momentum rolling as they enter their bye week after they host Vanderbilt under the lights on Saturday. Kentucky just played one of the best defenses in the SEC in Oklahoma , and now they get to play one of the worst as we previewed the Vanderbilt defense . On the offensive side of the football, the Commodores are led by five star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The offense has struggled but Curtis has shown plenty of flashes although he has a ton of room to grow. In our Vanderbilt defensive preview, we really centered it around Kentucky's offense and how they can exploit the Commodores defense. We are going to do the same here because this game is about Kentucky staying focused to enter the bye week with a 7-1 record. Jared Curtis has a rocket for an arm and is a big, physical runner. Kentucky head coach Will Stein said that Curtis plays like Josh Allen, but he made it clear he was not making the comparison. Coach Stein is correct though, Curtis can make unreal throws down the field and runs with physicality that is rare at the quarterback position. However, Curtis has a long way to become the dangerous player he is capable of. Curtis still needs to fix little things like footwork, staying in the pocket and taking care of the football. Curtis has one of the highest turnover worthy play percentages in the SEC, he will put the ball in harms way against this Kentucky defense that has been incredibly opportunistic this season. Curtis does not have much help around him, his offensive line has struggled all season. Vanderbilt allows the highest pressure rate in the SEC, which has led to Curtis being sacked a total of 10 times this season. However, Curtis is really difficult to bring down with his 6'4, 230-pound frame. His ability to erase sack opportunities is similar to South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers. Kentucky will win this matchup in the trenches, this deep defensive line unit will be able to get consistent pressure on Curtis. The biggest question will be how often they can convert those pressures into sacks, which they have been better at doing the last two weeks against Sam Leavitt and John Mateer. It will be a vital coaching point all week for the Wildcats to finish the play and get Curtis on the ground. If they allow Curtis to extend plays with his legs and erase sacks, it can lead to big plays down field as a passer or scrambling for a first down. Luckily for Kentucky, they won't have to see wide receiver Tre Richardson as he transferred to Louisville. Richardson lit them up last year down the field with Diego Pavia throwing all over this defense. I am sure a lot of the returning Wildcats on the defense have not forgotten that 45-17 beatdown last year in Nashville. This motivation will play a factor against a Vanderbilt team that is in a rebuilding stage. The Commodores receiving room is led by veteran Junior Sherrill, who is far and away the best weapon on this offense. Sherrill leads Vanderbilt in receptions, yards and touchdowns. He has four touchdowns on the season and all other wide receivers have combined for just one on the season. This is the guy to watch when Vanderbilt is on offense, they will force feed him the football. Vanderbilt offensive coordinator Tim Beck has one of the most unique offenses in the country and we saw how dangerous it could be last season. However, they lost their quarterback Diego Pavia who thrived in his system, they also lost their mismatch tight end Eli Stowers and the explosive weapon Richardson who transferred to Louisville. This is very much a transition year for this offense and it shows up on film. Kentucky has another opportunity to make a statement on defense after creating four turnovers and holding Oklahoma to just one touchdown last week. Kentucky Football continues to climb in the AP Top 25 Poll , moving up three spots to No. 12 after defeating Oklahoma, 21-13, in Norman. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 overall, became bowl eligible, and strengthened their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff in head coach Will Stein’s first season. The victory was far from perfect, as Kentucky’s offense struggled to find consistency after an impressive opening drive. However, the defense came up with several crucial plays down the stretch to help the Wildcats secure another impressive road win. Kentucky’s offense looked sharp on its opening possession, slicing through Oklahoma’s defense and setting the tone early. However, the unit stalled after that drive and did not score another offensive touchdown until 12:53 remained in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez for the Wildcats’ second touchdown of the game. Although the final score was relatively low, Kentucky’s defense also struggled at times in the first half. Safety Jordan Castell came up with a key interception when Oklahoma attempted a fake field goal in the first quarter, ending a promising Sooners possession. The Wildcats’ defense began to turn things around late in the third quarter when Ty Bryant intercepted Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer, giving Kentucky possession in Sooners territory. From there, the defense took control. Oklahoma recorded two three-and-outs and threw two more interceptions. Castell returned one for a pick-six, extending Kentucky’s lead to eight points, while Bryant secured the game-ending interception to seal the victory. While the game was sloppy on both sides, Kentucky found a way to finish strong. The Wildcats improved to 6-1, earned bowl eligibility, and continued building momentum as they pursue a potential College Football Playoff appearance. Now, Kentucky returns home to Kroger Field to face Vanderbilt, looking to avenge consecutive losses to the Commodores while losing three of four in the series. Kentucky fell 45-17 on the road last season after suffering a 20-13 defeat at home the year before. With Vanderbilt struggling through a disappointing season, the Wildcats will have an opportunity to extend their winning ways and continue climbing the national rankings. But if this last weekend showed us anything, it’s that upsets are commonplace this season, and Kentucky can’t afford to come out flat against a Commodores team starving for its first SEC win of the season. That, and Vandy did nearly pull off an upset over an Auburn team that just won at No. 1 Georgia. The Dores may be struggling, but they’ve still got an SEC roster. Vanderbilt Commodores (3-4, 0-4 in SEC) Vanderbilt has struggled through the first seven games of the season, and life after former quarterback Diego Pavia has been challenging. The Commodores finished the 2025 regular season with an impressive 10-2 record before losing to Iowa in the Citrus Bowl, ending the year at 10-3. However, the Dores have not come close to replicating that success this season. Vanderbilt suffered a disappointing 31-21 loss to Arkansas this past weekend. The Razorbacks entered the matchup on a 14-game Southeastern Conference losing streak, but they snapped that drought against the Commodores. One of Vanderbilt’s biggest challenges has been the development of 5-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The young signal-caller has shown flashes of his talent, but his inexperience has been evident. The drop-off from Pavia to Curtis has been noticeable, and Vanderbilt’s decision to start a true freshman at quarterback has come with growing pains. Through seven games, Curtis has completed 101/161 passes for 62.7%, totaling six passing touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 11 times. Curtis measures 6-foot-3 and weighs 230 pounds, giving him the physical tools to develop into a quality quarterback. He can also make plays with his legs, recording 55 carries for 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns. However, his turnover numbers and struggles under pressure will be areas Kentucky looks to exploit. Vanderbilt’s other major weakness has been its defense, particularly against the run. The Commodores have struggled to establish consistency along their front seven, which could create problems against Kentucky’s rushing attack. The Wildcats have a three-headed backfield featuring CJ Baxter, provided he is healthy enough to play, alongside Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. If Kentucky can keep all three involved, Vanderbilt could have a difficult time slowing down the ground game. Kentucky’s offensive line, known as the Big Blue Wall, has also looked impressive this season. If the unit continues to open running lanes and control the line of scrimmage, the Wildcats could have a significant advantage. As for Vanderbilt’s offense, Curtis has several weapons at his disposal. Senior wide receiver Junior Sherrill has emerged as Curtis’ primary target. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound receiver has recorded 41 receptions for 628 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. Junior wide receiver Ja’Cory Thomas provides another option at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds. He has recorded 12 receptions for 195 yards and one touchdown. Vanderbilt also features junior tight end Jayvontay Conner, who stands 6-foot-4 and weighs 235 pounds. Conner has totaled 13 receptions for 146 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown this season. Junior receiver Tristen Brown has added another option in the passing game, recording 12 receptions for 145 yards. In the backfield, Vanderbilt relies primarily on two running backs. Senior Sedrick Alexander, who stands 5-foot-9 and weighs 207 pounds, has recorded 61 carries for 270 yards and five touchdowns. Senior Makhilyn Young, at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, has added 52 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns. For Vanderbilt to pull off the upset, Curtis will need to protect the football, make better decisions under pressure, and find ways to move the ball against Kentucky’s defense. The Commodores will also need to improve against the run to keep the Wildcats’ offense from controlling the game. Kentucky, meanwhile, will look to establish the run early, protect Minchey, and continue creating turnovers defensively. With the Wildcats playing at home and Vanderbilt struggling in SEC play, Kentucky has an opportunity to deliver another convincing win against a team that’s had its number. How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Vanderbilt Commodores Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Time: 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24 TV Info: SEC Network Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as an 11.5-point favorite. ESPN gives Kentucky an 85.4% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 6-1 and bowl eligible, with its attention now turning toward the College Football Playoff. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have shown they can win in different ways, whether through explosive offensive performances or clutch defensive plays in lower-scoring games. Vanderbilt, meanwhile, is reeling after falling to 3-4 overall and 0-4 in SEC play. Losing to Arkansas after the Razorbacks had endured a 14-game conference losing streak raises further questions about the direction of the Commodores’ season. Kentucky also has extra motivation after losing to Vanderbilt in each of the past two seasons. With the Wildcats playing at home, an improving defense, and a rushing attack capable of taking control of the game, I expect Kentucky to avenge those losses and earn a convincing victory. picks.headline: How No. 12 Kentucky football and Vanderbilt match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey completed 21 of 28 passes for 158 yards and two touchdowns in the Wildcats’ 21-13 win at Oklahoma last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound transfer from Notre Dame has been a paragon of efficiency so far as a Wildcat. On the season, Minchey has completed 68.4% of his throws for 1,551 yards with 13 touchdowns vs. one interception . • Vanderbilt true freshman Jared Curtis is a player UK coach Will Stein sought to recruit while serving as Oregon offensive coordinator. “He’s very young,” Stein said of Curtis, “but in terms of the tangibles of the position, being able to throw it, arm talent, running strength, he is a prototype first-round-type talent.” A homegrown, 6-3, 230-pound Nashville product, Curtis is completing 62.7% of his throws for 1,242 yards and six touchdowns. Ball security has been an issue for the freshman QB, who has thrown seven interceptions and lost two fumbles. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky leading rusher CJ Baxter (484 yards, 5.6 yards a carry, eight touchdowns) sat out last week’s victory at Oklahoma with an undisclosed injury. In Baxter’s absence, third-year player Jason Patterson led UK with 38 yards on 12 carries vs. the Sooners. Former Oklahoma back Jovantae Barnes carried five times for 16 yards last week vs. his former team. • Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea deploys a two-man running back rotation. Senior Sedrick Alexander has run for 270 yards and five touchdowns and is averaging 4.4 yards a rush. The 5-9, 207-pound product of Austin, Texas, has also caught 11 passes for 94 yards and a score. Senior Makhilyn Young has rushed for 232 yards and two TDs and is averaging 4.2 yards a carry. A 5-10, 210-pound product of Midland, Texas, Young has caught 10 passes for 76 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky’s Kenny Darby was named a Midseason Freshman All-American by On3 Sports this week. The 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, leads UK with 34 catches and 436 receiving yards and is tied for the team lead with three touchdown receptions. Senior Nic Anderson made an acrobatic, juggling catch against Oklahoma — the team for whom he played as a freshman. Over the past three games, the 6-4, 205-pound Atlanta product has caught 13 passes. On the season, Anderson has 17 catches for 197 yards and a TD. • Vanderbilt senior Junior Sherrill is fourth in the SEC in receptions with 41. A 5-11, 200-pound Nashville product, Sherrill has 628 receiving yards and has caught four touchdown passes. In Vandy’s 45-17 strafing of UK last season, Sherrill caught eight passes for 115 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is putting together an All-SEC-caliber season. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School caught five passes for 38 yards and two touchdowns in last week’s win at Oklahoma. On the season, Rodriguez has 33 catches for 257 yards and three TDs. • A transfer from East Carolina who began his college career at Ole Miss, Vanderbilt’s Jayvontay Conner has 13 catches for 146 yards. Cole Spence has six receptions for 72 yards. In last season’s blowout of UK, Spence caught three passes for 48 yards. Offensive line • Kentucky left offensive tackle Lance Heard was named a First Team Mid-Season All-American this week by On3 Sports. A 6-6, 325-pound product of Bonita, Louisiana, Heard was recently ranked the 29th-best prospect for the 2027 NFL draft by CBSSports.com. • Vanderbilt “quick guard” Cade McConnell is the only returning starter along the offensive front from last season’s 10-3 team. A 6-5, 323-pound product of Choctaw, Oklahoma, McConnell began his college career at Minnesota. Center Lyndon Cooper logged 25 career starts at Pittsburgh and was considered a portal-recruiting coup for Vandy. Advantage: Kentucky Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace and tackle Tavion Gadson were disruptive forces for UK late in the win at Oklahoma. Humphrey-Grace, a 6-4, 271-pound senior from Cincinnati, was credited with 1.5 sacks and three quarterback hurries vs. the Sooners. It was Humphrey-Grace deflecting the ball off the throwing hand of Oklahoma QB John Mateer that set up the Ty Bryant interception that was the turning point in the game. Gadson, a 6-5, 303-pound junior from Savannah, Georgia, made eight tackles, 1.5 sacks and broke up a pass. “Those guys are really good players,” Will Stein said of Gadson and Humphrey-Grace. • At 6-7, 305 pounds, Vanderbilt tackle Issa Ouattara is an impactful presence in the interior of the Commodores’ defensive front. A product of Cologne, Germany, Ouattara has two sacks and three QB hurries so far in 2026. Edge Miles Capers leads Vandy with six tackles for loss and has two sacks, an interception and the forced fumble that set up Vanderbilt’s game-winning touchdown on the final play of a 35-31 victory over North Carolina State. • Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey made a game-high 15 tackles at Oklahoma. WLB Bo Barnes was not far behind with 10 stops. It has been a season of starts and stops for fifth-year player Alex Afari . The 6-2, 227-pound Cincinnati product is a member of the high school class of 2022 that the NCAA has attempted to exclude from the new 5-for-5 eligibility model. Afari was eligible for UK’s first four games due to a ruling in Jefferson County Circuit Court. However, the NCAA won on appeal at the Kentucky Court of Appeals, making Afari ineligible for the South Carolina and LSU games. A subsequent ruling by the Jefferson County Circuit Court last week restored Afari’s eligibility prior to the Oklahoma contest. The legal back-and-forth “is frustrating for him and for us,” Will Stein said. “We just got to roll with the punches a little bit. It’s out of our control. It’s out of his control at the end of the day, and he’s responded appropriately.” • Vanderbilt WLB Nick Rinaldi is a stat stuffer. A 6-3, 240-pound product of Dover, Massachusetts, Rinaldi has made 42 tackles, 5.5 TFL, 3.5 sacks and has hurried the quarterback four times and broken up passes four times. MLB Bryan Longwell is second on the team with 50 tackles. Longwell had a TFL in Vandy’s rout of UK last season. Advantage : Vanderbilt Defensive backs • Kentucky senior safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell each had two interceptions in the win over Oklahoma. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound transfer from Florida, foiled a Sooners’ fake field goal with an interception in the end zone and later returned a pick of John Mateer 41 yards for the game’s final touchdown. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Frederick Douglass High School alumnus, set up Kentucky’s go-ahead TD with a 42-yard interception return, then sealed the Wildcats’ victory with a pick with 21 seconds left in the game. • Vanderbilt strong safety CJ Heard leads the Commodores in tackles with 52. A 5-11, 210-pound Atlanta product who began his college career at Florida Atlantic, Heard also has made four tackles for loss, three sacks, broken up five passes, forced two fumbles and intercepted a pass. Special teams • Kentucky has not had consistently stellar punting in 2026, but Wilson Berry played a big role in the win at Oklahoma. The Australian uncorked a 58-yard, rugby-style kick that backed OU up to its 4-yard line with 2:43 left in the game. On the season, Berry is averaging 44 yards on eight punts and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line twice. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 8 of 11 on field goals in 2026 with a long make of 52 yards. • Vanderbilt punter Tyler Ebel is averaging 47 yards a kick and has pinned opponents inside their 20-yard line on 10 of 27 punts. Place-kicker Brock Taylor is 6 of 8 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 47 yards. For his college career, Taylor is 47 of 53 on field-goal tries with a long make of 57 yards. away.headline: Initial Vanderbilt football injury report before trip to No. 12 Kentucky
away.blurb: Vanderbilt football heads out of town to Lexington, Kentucky this weekend to take on the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats for its fifth SEC game. But before the game kicks off this weekend, we have to know who is going to be available Saturday night. Wednesday night, the SEC released its initial player availability reports leading up to this weekend’s slate of games. What was not know were the statuses of EDGE Brian Allen Jr., safety Dontae Carter and offensive lineman Mitchell Smith. On the first injury report, Allen Jr. is officially listed as out while Carter is listed as questionable and Smith is listed as probable. Tuesday, Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea announced that Allen Jr. did not practice due to an ankle injury, but Carter did practice wearing a no-contact jersey. In the case of Smith, Lea sounded hopeful Tuesday that he would be able to play after missing the last two games. In addition to those three, linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful for Saturday's game while safety Davin Chandler is listed as questionable. Along with Smith on the probable designation are cornerback Cayden Daniels and defensive lineman Hayden Bray. The Commodores are currently on a four-game losing streak and are the only team in the conference to not win a SEC game this season. Contrast that with Kentucky, who is currently one of the hottest teams in the country and firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation. Vanderbilt had a somewhat lengthy injury report. The Commodores already knew going into the week it was going to be missing backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, cornerback Jaylin Lackey, defensive lineman Aaron Bryant and offensive lineman Gunner Givens. In recent weeks, Lea announced season-ending injuries to Givens and Bryant and a collarbone injury to Berlowitz. Vanderbilt will continue to be without linebacker Jamison Curtis, wide receiver Kahden Smith and defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson Lea will likely give updates on his guys Thursday from tonight's injury report as he usually does. At this point in the year, Vanderbilt is fairly banged up. But it has its final game this weekend before the bye week. This weekend’s game between Vanderbilt and Kentucky is significant to both teams in different ways. One team is looking to get its confidence back while the other is looking to not slip up as a big favorite at home. The Commodores and Wildcats kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT on SEC Network. Nearly half the league is down to its backup quarterback, whether due to injury or by choice. The only undefeated team in the conference is UCLA , while Oregon's conference title hopes are hanging on by a thread. Ohio State just picked up a huge win, but faces the prospect of being without Julian Sayin for the rest of the season. It's chaos, and when chaos is around, there's a chance someone unexpected will emerge and take advantage of it. So while No. 16 USC's trip to Madison this weekend to face Wisconsin might not be the headliner game of the weekend, it's a chance for two teams to step forward and stake a claim in the conference. USC has won two straight since dropping a game to Oregon, and perhaps most surprisingly, one of those wins has come on the road. The Trojans are 2-0 outside the Coliseum, which has been a serious problem for them during Lincoln Riley's tenure. Now they're back on the road facing a Wisconsin team coming off its first Big Ten loss at UCLA last week. The winner stays in the Big Ten title race with a chance to capitalize on the chaos. The loser will have to hope for a lot more chaos to befall the rest of the league going forward. USC vs. Wisconsin: Need to know Wisconsin has struggled with USC: They haven't shared a conference for long, but there is familiarity with these programs. Familiarity Wisconsin would sooner forget. USC is 7-1 all time against the Badgers, with the lone loss coming in the 2015 Holiday Bowl. They've only played once as Big Ten foes, and USC won that game 38-21 in Los Angeles during the 2024 season. As for the trip to Camp Randall, USC has won both the games in Madison, though the last meeting came in 1965. NCAA eligibility rules change every day, but I'm pretty sure none of the players who played in that game have remaining eligibility. Lincoln Riley is good off a bye: While Wisconsin was in Los Angeles losing to UCLA last week, USC was in Los Angeles chilling on the couch watching. That's typically been a good thing for the Trojans. Under Lincoln Riley, USC is 5-1 coming off a bye and has won three straight. Wisconsin has performed poorly in these spots of late: Wisconsin has played six home games against AP-ranked opponents under Luke Fickell. It has won only once in those six games. That win came last season against No. 24 Washington . As for the five losses, four of them have come by at least 14 points, though all four of them were against top-4 teams in the poll. If there was any time to wish for temperatures in the 40s with biting wind, it's when USC is coming to town. Instead, the forecast is calling for temperatures in the 60s with a manageable breeze. Still, even if the weather won't have an oversized impact, I like the under here. USC may have won its two road trips so far this season, but the offense didn't look great against Penn State , and this Wisconsin defense is good. I also don't have much faith in the Wisconsin offense. Stylz Blackmon, who had been playing right guard, moved to center to replace Kawecki, while PJ Wilkins slotted into guard. Now, Kawecki has been upgraded to ‘Probable’ ahead of the Badgers’ matchup with the Trojans. Kawecki’s return would be a nice boost for the offensive line that struggled mightily against UCLA last week. A pair of starters are ‘questionable’ for Saturday Two starters popped up on the report this week that we didn’t expect. Wide receiver Malachi Coleman and cornerback Javan Robinson are both listed as ‘questionable’ for Saturday. RB Nate Palmer remains ‘doubtful’ The Badgers got Abu Sama back off the injury report last week, but injuries remain at the position. After missing last week’s game against UCLA, Nate Palmer remains ‘doubtful’ for this week’s game. Palmer has received only a handful of carries this season, but he has been a constant presence on special teams and the team’s primary kick returner, returning six kicks for an average of 28.2 yards per return. Christian Borman Oct 22, 2026 Share Wisconsin Badgers wide receiver Malachi Coleman. Photo credit: UW Athletics The Wisconsin football team has released its initial availability report ahead of its matchup with USC this Saturday evening. Some players are trending in the right direction after missing time, but a couple of names on the report weren’t expected. Here’s where things stand three days ahead of the matchup with the Trojans. Austin Kawecki is trending in the right direction Starting center Austin Kawecki left in the middle of the Badgers’ game with Michigan State in Week 5. With a bye week to rest, there was hope he would be back for the Badgers’ road game against UCLA in Week 7. Javan Robinson has been the most consistent cornerback for the Badgers this season. If he misses the game, it would be a massive blow to the defense, especially in a week when they face one of the best passing quarterbacks in the country, Jordan Maiava. On top of that, the cornerback depth has already taken a hit this year after Cai Bates was lost for the season with a knee injury early in the year. Losing Coleman wouldn’t be ideal, either. But the passing attack for the Badgers has been inconsistent, and even after his breakout game against Notre Dame in Week 1, he hasn’t been the force we all hoped he’d be. Fortunately for the Badgers, they just got Jaylon Domingeaux back from injury last week and caught a pair of passes, so there is at least some more depth at receiver. away.blurb: Williams camped out in the back of his team's end zone on a long kick just before halftime and made the most of his opportunity as he snagged a missed field goal off the leg of Joe McFadden. Polasek's Bison joined the Football Bowl Subdivision, also known as Division-I, earlier this July. The Bison were ranked in recent NCAA Top 25 Power Rankings but fell out this week . North Dakota State’s Jackson Williams returns missed field goal for insane 100 yard touchdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Nick Meyer, ClutchPoints Sun, October 18, 2026 at 5:54 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The North Dakota State Bison welcomed the Nevada Wolfpack to Fargodome in Fargo, North Dakota and won 31-17 in a FBS showdown among two Mountain West teams . Bison coach Tim Polasek is now on a seven-year deal and looking to make a splash in FBS, something his kick returner Jackson Williams was able to do in Week 7. McFadden's 57-yard bomb fell short, giving Williams a chance to work his magic. CBS Sports shared video of the Play of the Year candidate, which helped NDSU open up a solid lead before halftime. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bison have continued their pursuit of excellence amid their step up in competition as they now sit at 3-1 in the Mountain West Conference, 6-1 overall. Their sterling conference record has them tied with the Air Force Falcons and Wyoming Cowboys for first place in the conference, with more challenges on the horizon for later this season. Week 8 brings a road game against the New Mexico Lobos, followed by a home date with the UTEP Miners in Week 9. A road trip to Hawaii will give Polasek's team a chance to get away from the cold, and will be followed up with games against Northern Illinois and San Jose State to finish the season. College football is now a national sport, and the rise of the Bison has shown how far a program can go with the right vision and the right leadership. Williams' signature play showed that North Dakota State is a team to be reckoned with, and a well-coached team capable of taking advantage of its opportunities on a grand scale. home.headline: Laubstein will miss rest of Lobos' season after suffering knee injury at Hawaii
home.blurb: After initially exhausting his eligibility, Laubstein was able to return to UNM for a sixth and final year via an NCAA waiver. A former junior college athlete, he successfully contended that at least one of his seasons spent at that level shouldn’t count toward his NCAA eligibility. James Laubstein, middle, provided a "lot of juice" for UNM, coach Jason Eck said. Mike Sandoval/Journal “Him being one of the oldest guys in the room, he taught me a lot,” Fa’avae said Tuesday. “(Laubstein) showed me the ropes and what to do, what not to do, how I should approach this, how I should approach that as a young quarterback. He taught me a lot of stuff I know today and always had my back, always helped me out. … It’s sad that got his season (taken) from him.” “We’ll have to have some element of (the) quarterback run involved,” he added. “But we gotta be careful because now two of our top four quarterbacks (Laubstein and Layne) coming into the year are out. So you don’t wanna get to less than that, you know?” Eck indicated receiver Shawn Miller (concussion) is not likely to play this week: “He’s just not coming along. He’s still battling symptoms and stuff, so he has not cleared the protocol (to return). And the longer it goes on, I think the more concerning it is because I think when you (show symptoms over an extended period of time), that kind of shows that it’s really affecting you. And that calls into question, is it safe for you to play?” Jump to main content NM Data Scoreboard Run-first QB had 5 rushing TDs, the second-best mark for UNM James Laubstein, right, had a knack for finding the end zone with his legs. He rushed for five this season before his injury at Hawaii, including on in the Lobos' blowout of UTEP on Oct. 3. Mike Sandoval/Journal Sean Reider Sean Reider Journal Staff Writer Published October 21, 2026 - 8:38 p.m. James Laubstein has played his last snap as a Lobo. New Mexico’s run-first backup quarterback suffered a season-ending knee injury in Saturday’s 21-10 win at Hawaii, coach Jason Eck said Monday. The 6-foot-3, 209-pound sixth-year player went down on a play in the second quarter and was later carted off the field with what Eck said was a patellar tendon injury. He rushed for 88 yards and five touchdowns — the second-best mark on the team — in his third and final season with the Lobos. Apologies for the bad video. Before Laubstein was carted off, he repeatedly screamed “LET’S GO” at the rest of the team. https://t.co/OqT7SdgWQA pic.twitter.com/xqzhB42EwL Laubstein underwent surgery Monday, Eck said. “Losing James is a big blow,” he added. “He’s been just dominating his role all year. Even that play (Laubstein was injured on), he gets a 12-yard run on his last play. “So, we’re going to miss James. James brought a lot of leadership, a lot of juice to the team and it’s a shame to lose him.” Upon returning to UNM, Laubstein competed with quarterbacks Toa Fa’avae and Luke Moga for the starting job in Jack Layne’s absence.
